Wider Sports News.title: Can US$300m investment, player equity and team stake sales save LIV Golf?
Wider Sports News.summary: Speaking alongside new investor BC Partners, LIV Golf chief executive Scott O’Neil set out the league’s path out of bankruptcy protection and explained why it is doubling down on its team-based structure to win over players and attract further capital. The post Can US$300m investment, player equity and team stake sales save LIV Golf? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Plenty has been said and written about the origins of LIV Golf, its finances and eventual demise. Yet in chief executive Scott O’Neil, LIV has an experienced administrator who is adamant that there is plenty of reason for optimism that ‘LIV 2.0’ can be a sustainable success.

After Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) pulled the plug in April, O’Neil went about securing the support of players and partners to finish the season before turning his attention to a new business plan that would allow LIV to continue without its benefactor. Filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy gave it the breathing room to pursue a new path and now it has signed up BC Partners as its first investor in a deal that could be worth up to US$300 million.

Wider Sports News.title: Euroleague confirms franchise plans: What now for its NBA grand alliance?
Wider Sports News.summary: EuroLeague, the elite club competition for European club basketball, has voted through a major overhaul of its financial structures and reportedly turned down an initial offer to work with the NBA on its long-mooted continental property. However, while both sides are pursuing independent plans, the prospect of a partnership remains on the table. The post Euroleague confirms franchise plans: What now for its NBA grand alliance? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Euroleague has confirmed plans for an overhaul of its financial and governance system – potentially reigniting a contest for the future of European basketball in the process. The 13 permanent shareholder clubs in the pancontinental competition voted at a meeting in Italy to move from a licensing model to franchises. Reuters reports they also concurrently turned down an offer to collaborate with the National Basketball Association (NBA).

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the NBA had made its proposal conditional on Euroleague moving away from plans to create franchises and expand to 24 teams. The US-based world leader has trailed a long-awaited update on its own 16-team European league, which it aims to launch in 2027 with the support of the International Basketball Federation (Fiba).

Wider Sports News.title: SportAccord heads to Africa for first time as Cape Town lands 2028 convention
Wider Sports News.summary: News comes in same week that South Africa named among seven countries interested in hosting 2036 Olympic Games. The post SportAccord heads to Africa for first time as Cape Town lands 2028 convention appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Cape Town in South Africa will host the SportAccord Convention in 2028, marking the first time the event has been staged in Africa. SportAccord’s flagship event, which brings together federations, host cities and other stakeholders across international sport, will be the latest sports event to be staged in Cape Town.

The South African city staged matches during the 2010 Fifa World Cup and more recently hosted games at the 2023 ICC Women’s T20 World Cup, including the final. Cape Town will follow Baku, which is hosting SportAccord from 9th to 13th May next year after the 2026 edition in the Azerbaijan capital was postponed. Birmingham staged the event in 2024.

Wider Sports News.title: Qatar Stars League makes financial sustainability central to its growth strategy
Wider Sports News.summary: QSL executive Ahmed Abbassi outlines how financial controls, commercial growth and rising fan engagement are shaping the league’s chapter. The post Qatar Stars League makes financial sustainability central to its growth strategy appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The Qatar Stars League (QSL) is putting financial sustainability at the centre of its strategy as it seeks to strengthen the league’s competitive and commercial position in an increasingly competitive Gulf football market.

Since 2021, the league has placed greater emphasis on building a sustainable competition, supported by stronger financial controls at club level. The principle is straightforward: clubs should not commit to player or coach contracts without having the budget to support them, while contracts should remain within market value.

Wider Sports News.title: Guido Klomp joins Two Circles to lead Benelux growth
Wider Sports News.summary: Appointment will support Two Circles’ ambition to help sports organisations across the Benelux better understand their fans and turn that understanding into sustainable growth The post Guido Klomp joins Two Circles to lead Benelux growth appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Amsterdam, 6 October 2026, Two Circles has appointed Guido Klomp as Managing Director Benelux, as it continues to expand its work with sports organisations across the region. Klomp joins from TBWA\NEBOKO, where he was heading the business of Dark Horses. Prior to this, he spent almost a decade as Director of Triple Double, later Golazo Brands, advising brands and rights holders including UEFA, PSV, ING Bank, KLM, Philips, Albert Heijn and Red Bull on sports business and commercial growth.

In his new role, Klomp will lead Two Circles’ Benelux business, bringing together its capabilities across data, technology, strategy and marketing to help sports organisations better understand their fans and translate that understanding into long-term value.

More than 160 teams from over 40 countries have already registered, surpassing the scale of the 2024 championships in Graz, Austria. Wider Sports News.title: ‘Sham’ contracts and inflated sponsorship revenue: What next for Man City after landmark Premier League verdict?
Wider Sports News.summary: As the club maintain their innocence, the sporting, commercial and financial effects have only begun to reverberate. The post ‘Sham’ contracts and inflated sponsorship revenue: What next for Man City after landmark Premier League verdict? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The story of the biggest financial scandal in English soccer history is by now a familiar saga, but it has not lost its capacity to shock. Last week, reports started to emerge that Manchester City had been found guilty by an independent commission of 114 of the 115 charges levelled against the club in 2023 for extensive breaches of its cost-control rules. Those leaks meant that when the Premier League’s official confirmation eventually arrived on 29th September, it came as no surprise.

But the scale of City’s deception and the severity of the language in both the league’s statement was unprecedented. The investigation determined City worked to ‘artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than UK£900 million’ between 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, a period in which they won three of their eight Premier League titles.

Rugby.body:
Harlequins boss Jason Gilmore is set to get a much-needed boost after passing England fly-half Marcus Smith fit for Sunday afternoon’s trip to Sale Sharks. Quins sit bottom of the Gallagher PREM, still seeking their first point of the season after defeats to Bath and Gloucester, who thrashed them 48-0, the club’s heaviest league defeat in 26 years.

But under-fire Gilmore will have Smith available for the first time since he damaged a finger in a friendly against Edinburgh, while England loosehead Fin Baxter is still being held back following a long-term foot injury.

Rugby.title: Brazil Women Sevens name new head coach after Crystal Kaua exit
Rugby.summary: Crystal Kaua has left her role as Brazil Women's Sevens head coach after the union opted not to renew the New Zealander's contract.
Rugby.body:
Crystal Kaua has left her role as Brazil Women’s Sevens head coach after the union opted not to renew the New Zealander’s contract. The former Chiefs Manawa head coach joined Brazil in 2024 and oversaw the team’s ninth-place finish at the HSBC SVNS World Championship in 2026. She was the first woman to coach the team.

Her tenure also included a dramatic HSBC SVNS 2 victory in São Paulo earlier in 2026. The victory clinched Brazil’s place at the SVNS World Championship, where they narrowly missed out on qualification for the HSBC SVNS Series.

They thumped Harlequins 48-0 at the weekend after beginning the campaign with a 45-24 victory at Exeter. Deacon, who joined Gloucester in April from Leicester Tigers, is now preparing to return to his former club on Friday to compete for the Slater Cup.

Rugby.title: How to solve a problem like Harlequins
Rugby.summary: It may sound like hyperbole this early in the season but Sunday’s visit to Sale might just be Harlequins’ biggest game since they last reached the play-offs four years ago.
Rugby.body:
It may sound like hyperbole this early in the season but Sunday’s visit to Sale might just be Harlequins’ biggest game since they last reached the play-offs four years ago. Since then they have been on a steady downward curve and Saturday’s embarrassing defeat at Kingsholm, their worst in the league for 26 years, may not prove to be the nadir as it’s hard to see where a win is coming from in the PREM until at least the New Year.

They could raise the level for their cup final in the London derby or catch Exeter or Leicester on an off day but their squad doesn’t compare well on paper and the fixture at Newcastle, who have levelled up along with a couple of other teams who didn’t fare well last season, on January 2 looks massive already.

Rugby.title: Celtic Challenge announces 2026/27 fixtures as competition continues to grow
Rugby.summary: Fixtures for the 2026/27 Celtic Challenge season have been announced, with the competition set to return for its fifth year in December.
Rugby.body:
Fixtures for the 2026/27 Celtic Challenge season have been announced, with the competition set to return for its fifth year in December. The new season will begin on Saturday 5 December and comprise 10 rounds, culminating on Saturday 27 February. The final will take place on the weekend of 27 March 2027.

For the first time, the highest-seeded team will host the final. Previous editions have seen the showpiece played at a neutral venue, but the highest seed of the two semi-final winners will now have home advantage.

Rugby.title: 'Long time coming'
Rugby.summary: After two years playing at the Aviva, Leinster return to their more 'intimate' home where they enjoyed a formidable winning record.
Rugby.body:
Late last year, huddled beside a radiator in the ornate but cavernous Grand Hall, I sat down with Johnny Sexton for a chat about his playing days, retirement and how rugby lured him back as a coach. Sexton was there as, 100 metres away, Laya Arena opened up to guests and reporters for the first time. The venue, known to sports fans as The RDS for years, was nearing the end of a two-year revamp. Leinster, his old club, would be returning there for the 2026-27 season.

“It’s been a long time coming, for Leinster to have a world-class ground,” Sexton commented. “It’s very much going to be like that, but it still retains that intimate sense of the RDS, in terms of how close the crowd are to the pitch.”

Rugby.summary: The DHL Stormers will be looking to make amends for the low point of last season when they welcome the table-topping Hollywoodbets Sharks to Cape Town for a “Test match” showdown on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
The DHL Stormers will be looking to make amends for the low point of last season when they welcome the table-topping Hollywoodbets Sharks to Cape Town for a “Test match” showdown on Saturday.

John Dobson’s team were beaten twice by the Sharks in the BKT URC in the space of seven dark days back in January, losing 30-19 at home and then 36-24 in Durban a week later. So they will be on a revenge mission at a packed DHL Stadium this weekend having selected a star-studded squad for the big South African derby.

Rugby.title: Why the Welsh ex-pat contingent should give Steve Tandy hope
Rugby.summary: The early season form of a clutch of Welsh men in England should give Steve Tandy cause for optimism with the Nations Championship fast-approaching
Rugby.body:
The late, great Mervyn Davies once fondly recalled how he had been part of a group of London-based Wales internationals who would rise at 4am, pile into a classic Mini and bomb across the border for national squad training.

Travelling with the 6ft 5in Merve the Swerve were club-mates JPR Williams, John Taylor, John Dawes and Mike Roberts, all sardined into the tiny car, with Geoff Evans occasionally making the Sunday trip depending on selection. They would train with Wales before driving straight back to London to be at their day jobs on Monday morning.

Rugby.summary: Exeter boss Rob Baxter says he has been impressed with how young Wales back-row Kane James is maturing.
Rugby.body:
Exeter boss Rob Baxter says he has been impressed with how young Wales back-row Kane James is maturing. The 21-year-old won his international first cap in July when Wales lost in Argentina in the Nations Championship.

James broke into the Exeter squad last season and has started both of the Chiefs' Prem games so far this campaign. "He's just following that really nice route where he's improving at a nice rate, he's having some good impact on games," Baxter said.

Rugby.title: Kenya Shujaa, Lionesses ready to face strong international challengers
Rugby.summary: Clubs from nine nations are set to converge on one of the biggest weekends of sevens rugby in Africa.
Rugby.body:
Clubs from nine nations are set to converge on one of the biggest weekends of sevens rugby in Africa, as the 2026 Safari Sevens gets underway this weekend. Six women’s teams and 12 men’s teams are set to do battle across the weekend, with several international invitational sides also set to take part at Nyayo Stadium in Nairobi.

First contested in 1996, this year marks the 30th anniversary of the landmark sevens tournament, with this weekend marking the 28th iteration of the tournament after no event was held in 2017 and during the COVID pandemic.

Rugby.summary: Speaking with reporters after announcing his matchday 23 for the Test, Rennie cut straight to the point when addressing Lomax's omission.
Rugby.body:
Dave Rennie has delivered a blunt explanation for the absence of Tyrel Lomax’s name in the All Blacks‘ team to play the Wallabies at Eden Park this weekend. Lomax has been considered New Zealand’s premier tighthead prop for much of the past five years, but a recent run of injuries has hampered his form and he’s struggled to make his mark in the international season to date.

As a result, Fletcher Newell has been backed in the No.3 jersey and will square off with Australia’s Angus Bell at scrum time in Auckland before Pasilio Tosi enters the match off the bench.

Rugby.title: Rugby Union Weekly
Rugby.summary: Danny and Sara chat to Irish rugby legend Peter O’Mahony about his illustrious career.
Rugby.body: Irish rugby legend Peter O’Mahony joins Danny and Sara for a special episode reflecting on his extraordinary career. We discuss World Cup heartbreaks, Six Nations success, and the sacrifices he made over 20 years as a pro. O’Mahony gives a fascinating insight into how Joe Schmidt transformed Ireland and unlocked a different level in him, and how team and environment has evolved since Andy Farrell took charge. He tells us how he was deeply affected by the tragic passing of Anthony Foley and how it changed him as a person and a rugby player. We hear how he bonded with Jamie George on the Lions tour in 2017 and why you should think twice before asking Ma’a Nonu for an All Blacks jersey. We also talk rivalries and quiz O’Mahony on his beef with Scotland.

Rugby.summary: 2026 Asian Games rugby sevens champions decided in thrilling finals Rugbypass.com

The rugby sevens at the 2026 Asian Games saw two thrilling days of action at Paloma Mizuho Rugby Stadium in Japan – and despite several emerging nations showing promise, the most developed rugby nations in Asia ultimately came through with the results.

Hong Kong China and Japan claimed gold in the men’s and women’s tournaments, respectively, both overcoming the People’s Republic of China, who finished with the two silver medals in each event.

Under-fire Harlequins boss Jason Gilmore insists he is the right man to halt the decline and bring the good times back to the Stoop, but says his critics need to be patient. Gilmore reiterated his side’s performance at Kingsholm was ‘unacceptable’ when he faced the media again on Wednesday but said there are no easy overnight fixes for the club’s decline since their shock PREM Final win in 2021.

Rugby.body:
The All Blacks have suffered another injury setback ahead of their Bledisloe Cup series, with Richie Mo’unga and Fehi Fineanganofo both ruled out of the meeting at Eden Park on Saturday.

Rugby.title: Compulsory media duties like something in an autocracy
Rugby.summary: Saracens' Brendan Venter compares Prem Rugby's media obligations to "something from an autocratic land" after reluctantly speaking at a press conference.
Rugby.body:
Saracens' Brendan Venter compared Prem Rugby's media obligations to "something from an autocratic land" after he made a reluctant appearance at a press conference. The 56-year-old returned to a full-time role at the club in the summer, initially as director of rugby, but has since been given an updated job title of head of culture and technical director.

His no-show at a pre-season media event cost Saracens a £5,000 fine and he avoided questions before and after the club's opening-round win over Leicester. However, he appeared alongside head coach Joe Shaw to preview this Saturday's match against Bristol and, after initially offering only short answers to reporters' questions, railed against the expectation that he would be the public face of the club.

Rugby.title: Can late-bloomer Maxime Lucu be France’s number one No.9 in Nations Championship?
Rugby.summary: With Antoine Dupont no longer an automatic choice at scrum-half, Bordeaux's Maxime Lucu could take centre stage in November.
Rugby.body:
Roll the clock back to 21 September 2023. In the 45th minute of a pool game between France and Namibia, Johan Deysel made a coruscating head-high hit on superstar scrum-half Antoine Dupont. The Toulousain magician left the field holding the side of his face and a rugby nation audibly held its breath. The match was supposed to be a group-stage cakewalk – it finished 96-0 to France – but the profundity of its impact rumbled around the rest of the competition like a distant thunderclap in an echo-chamber.

One day later, the full extent of the damage was revealed: a maxillo-zygomatic fracture, or a broken cheekbone to the likes of you and me. It seemed impossible that Dupont could be ready for a quarter-final against the reigning world champions, and the most aggressively physical team on planet rugby in only three weeks’ time. But ready he was – ‘Touché, mais pas coulé’ as Dupont himself wrote, referencing a popular naval combat game: ‘Hit, but not sunk’.

Rugby.title: Ireland must ‘thrive’ in physical South Africa challenge
Rugby.summary: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand is relishing the challenge of testing his team against South Africa in a two-match tour as part of WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
Ireland head coach Scott Bemand is relishing the challenge of testing his team against South Africa in a two-match tour as part of the WXV Global Series. So far in the WXV Global Series, Ireland have lost to the USA Women’s Eagles and beaten Japan 31-24. In a second game against the Sakura Fifteen, played outside of the WXV Global Series window, Ireland were 43-19 winners in Cork.

But across their autumn fixtures, Ireland have struggled for consistency, turned over the ball regularly and given away more penalties than any head coach would have liked. They have hardly put out the rip-roaring performances we saw for swathes of this year’s Guinness Women’s Six Nations.

Rugby.summary: Having earned promotion from the bench midway through the Guinness Six Nations, Carter went on to make six successive starts for his country.
Rugby.body:
To get an insight into the qualities which have seen Ben Carter nail down a Wales second row spot, it’s revealing to listen to his Dragons RFC coach Filo Tiatia. Having earned promotion from the bench midway through the Guinness Six Nations, Carter went on to make six successive starts for his country, establishing himself as a key cog in the machine.

He has brought a huge defensive work-rate – as illustrated by him winning the BKT URC Tackle Machine award last season – along with hard carrying, all-round physicality and lineout acumen.

Rugby.title: France's Emmanuel Meafou signs huge deal
Rugby.summary: France lock Emmanuel Meafou has signed a five-year contract extension with Toulouse, keeping him at the Top 14 champions until 2032.
Rugby.body:
France lock Emmanuel Meafou has signed a five-year contract extension with Toulouse, keeping him at the Top 14 champions until 2032. The 28-year-old was due to come out of contract next summer and had reportedly attracted strong interest from Stade Français, but has instead committed his long-term future to the club he joined from Australia in 2019.

Meafou has become one of Toulouse’s key forwards during his time at Stade Ernest-Wallon, winning two European titles and five Top 14 crowns. He has also established himself with France since becoming eligible in 2023, earning 18 caps and featuring in their 2025 and 2026 Six Nations title-winning campaigns.

Rugby.title: Bath attack coach Mike Prendergast: 'I've a very strong relationship with Finn'
Rugby.summary: Most coaches would count themselves fortunate to work with a generational talent like Finn Russell once in their career in club rugby, few get the chance to do it twice.
Rugby.body:
Most coaches would count themselves fortunate to work with a generational talent like Finn Russell once in their career in club rugby, few get the chance to do it twice. No wonder Bath’s new attack coach Mike Prendergast seemed very happy with his lot when chatting enthusiastically to the media on Tuesday for the first time since his move from Munster.

You get the impression that Prendergast would never run out of good things to say about Russell, who he coached previously at Racing 92 and believes has matured into an even more well-rounded player in his three and a bit seasons at Bath, which is a good thing considering a team’s attack coach and 10 need to singing from the same hymn sheet. Apparently, Prendergast can hold a tune as well as Russell can hold a defence.

Rugby.title: Munster act swiftly in appointing interim CEO
Rugby.summary: Munster have appointed former Hurricanes chief executive Avan Lee as their interim CEO as the province prepares for Ian Flanagan’s departure at the end of October.
Rugby.body:
Munster have appointed former Hurricanes chief executive Avan Lee as their interim CEO as the province prepares for Ian Flanagan’s departure at the end of October. Lee will take up the position towards the end of the month, less than a year after ending a decade-long spell in charge of the Wellington-based Super Rugby side.

The 10-year tenure included the Hurricanes’ first Super Rugby title in 2016, while the franchise went on to win Super Rugby Pacific again in 2026, several months after Lee had stepped down. He left the role last November following changes at board level and wider developments within the organisation.

Rugby.title: World Rugby announce new crackdown on two dangerous tackles
Rugby.summary: World Rugby have moved to outlaw two dangerous tackle techniques, with changes covering the 'hip drop' and 'knee drop' set to come into force over the coming weeks.
Rugby.body:
World Rugby have moved to outlaw two dangerous tackle techniques, with changes covering the ‘hip drop’ and ‘knee drop’ set to come into force over the coming weeks. The governing body have confirmed that the ‘hip drop’ tackle will be explicitly added to Law 9.13, which covers dangerous play, from November 1. The offence will carry a sanction of at least a penalty.

A ‘hip drop’ occurs when a tackler uses their bodyweight to pull a ball-carrier to ground before dropping onto the player’s legs from behind. World Rugby have also issued guidance on the ‘knee drop’, where a defender drops to one or both knees before making contact.

Rugby.title: Why the Bledisloe Cup has the heritage and edge to match the RGR
Rugby.summary: For so long, a ding-dong rivalry, if the Wallabies renaissance can continue, the Bledisloe Cup has the kudos to rival RGR
Rugby.body:
For at least two generations of New Zealanders, there was no sense that the All Blacks’ greatest rival was the Springboks. For those born in the 1980s, the Wallabies were New Zealand’s great rival and for much of the 1990s, they were in fact the All Blacks’ nemesis. Come the big moments and the big games, it would be the Wallabies who had the rugby smarts and calm heads to win them.

It was a different time. The Wallabies, on the back of their Grand Slam-winning team of 1984 transformed into a genuine heavyweight. They won the Bledisloe Cup in 1986 and while they lost it the following year in a one-off Test, they became a super competitive force for the next 15 years.

Rugby.body:
Leicester Tigers have confirmed the sad news that Finn Theobald-Thomas has been forced to retire from rugby with immediate effect on medical grounds. The 23-year-old hooker joined Tigers ahead of the 2023-24 season, having previously played for Worcester and Gloucester, and made 33 appearances for the club.

His last appearance was seven months ago, as a replacement for Jamie Blamire in the Slater Cup tie against Gloucester at Villa Park, a game the Tigers won with a bonus point. Theobald-Thomas, who is being supported by the Rugby Players’ Association and Leicester as he begins the transition into retirement, played all the way through the age groups for England.

Rugby.summary: Two-time Women's Six Nations winner Gill Bourke has joined Leicester Tigers coaching staff ahead of the 2026/27 Premiership Women's Rugby season.
Rugby.body:
Two-time Women’s Six Nations winner Gill Bourke has joined Leicester Tigers’ coaching staff ahead of the 2026/27 Premiership Women’s Rugby season. The 42-year-old former front-row spent her playing career with Munster, UL Bohemians, Stade Français, Harlequins and Loughborough Lightning.

She also represented Ireland at Women’s Rugby World Cups in 2010 and 2014, and earned 51 caps for her country in a seven-year Test career. Rugby.title: Sale Sharks enforcer Jacques Vermeulen learns his fate after red card
Rugby.summary: The South African has been ruled out for the remainder of October after being hit with a four-match ban.
Rugby.body:
Sale Sharks back rower Jacques Vermeulen has been handed a four-match ban after being given a 20-minute red card during Sunday’s hard-fought 21-17 win over Saracens at the StoneX Stadium.

The 31-year-old made contact with the head of Saracens scrum-half Tomos Williams in the 18th minute as he tried to clear out a ruck, and after a TMO intervention, was sent off to leave Sharks with 13 men, following Alex Lozowski’s earlier sin-binning for a high shot on Alfie Barbeary.

James Lightfoot Brown will oversee the attack, Adam Powell the defence, James Craig the forwards and Nathan Catt the scrum when England A begin their 2026/27 programme in Bath on November 6.

Lightfoot Brown, Powell and Craig were all involved in last season’s matches against All Blacks XV, Spain and Ireland XV, while Catt has previously worked with the A side against Australia A and Spain. Lightfoot Brown coaches at Gloucester, Powell at Saracens and Craig at Northampton Saints, while Catt works in the pathway.

Rugby.summary: Sale Sharks boss Alex Sanderson is ready to fight to keep “mega athlete” Wales international Christ Tshiunza at the club next season, amid interest from Welsh regions, with a move potentially helping him kick-start his international career.
Rugby.body:
Sale Sharks boss Alex Sanderson is ready to fight to keep “mega athlete” Wales international Christ Tshiunza at the club next season, amid interest from Welsh regions, with a move potentially helping him kick-start his international career.

Tshiunza, 24, who plays lock and openside flanker, moved to the Sharks on a one-year deal from Exeter Chiefs this summer but is 10 caps short of meeting the controversial 25-cap threshold that would make him eligible for selection by Steve Tandy.

Rugby.title: Carwyn Tuipulotu makes immediate effect move to Gallagher PREM
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs have signed former Scarlets and Pau No.8 Carwyn Tuipulotu with immediate effect, strengthening Rob Baxter’s options at the start of the Gallagher PREM season.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs have signed former Scarlets and Pau No.8 Carwyn Tuipulotu with immediate effect, strengthening Rob Baxter’s options at the start of the Gallagher PREM season. The 24-year-old arrives as a free agent after leaving Top 14 side Pau during the summer and has most recently been training with the Dragons to maintain his fitness ahead of finding a new club.

The former Wales U20 international, who can operate across the back-row but specialises at No. 8, previously made more than 45 appearances for the Scarlets before spending part of the 2024/25 season on loan at Saracens and then moving to France.

Rugby.title: Talks taking place over Glasgow Warriors' future at Scotstoun
Rugby.summary: Glasgow Warriors are hoping to secure their future at Scotstoun until at least 2032, with talks about extending their current lease ongoing.
Rugby.body:
Glasgow Warriors are hoping to secure their future at Scotstoun until at least 2032, with talks about extending their current lease ongoing. As things stand, the Warriors’ lease runs until 2028, but in an interview with Scotland Rugby News, Warriors managing director Kenny Brown confirmed a new four-year deal is close to be finalised with Glasgow Life – the leisure arm of Glasgow City Council.

Glasgow have called Scotstoun home since 2012 and there has been a feeling in recent times that the 2016 Pro12 champions and 2024 URC winners have outgrown the venue, which only has a capacity of 7,261, although that increased to 11,000 when it hosted a scaled-back Commonwealth Games this summer.

Rugby.title: Swys de Bruin's post-Springbok Women role has been confirmed
Rugby.summary: Swys de Bruin has taken up his first coaching role since leaving his position as Springbok Women head coach last month.
Rugby.body:
Swys de Bruin has taken up his first coaching role since leaving his position as Springbok Women head coach last month. The 66-year-old has joined Paarl Boys’ High School as their head of coaching.

It is a position that his son, Neil, vacated in December 2025 to join the Blue Bulls as their attack coach in the United Rugby Championship. At the start of September, ahead of the Springbok Women’s clash with the Black Ferns in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, it was confirmed that De Bruin had abruptly vacated his role as head coach.

Rugby.title: Henry Pollock addresses LA28 Olympic rumours head on
Rugby.summary: Henry Pollock has said that representing Great Britain Sevens at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics is “definitely something I’m aspiring to do”.
Rugby.body:
Henry Pollock has said that representing Great Britain Sevens at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics is “definitely something I’m aspiring to do”. The Northampton Saints and England back-row has been linked with a place in a prospective Great Britain squad alongside Marcus Smith, Tommy Freeman, Henry Arundell and Noah Caluori. RugbyPass reported in July that the quintet had been targeted with LA28 in mind.

Pollock’s immediate priority remains next year’s Rugby World Cup in Australia, but, speaking during a Q&A on his YouTube channel, the 21-year-old made no secret of the appeal of following the path taken by Antoine Dupont, who switched his focus to sevens before helping France win Olympic gold on home soil in Paris in 2024.

Rugby.title: 'Rugby needs to be demystified to attract new fans and fresh investment'
Rugby.summary: The inaugural Nations Championship represents the first major opportunity to embrace private investment, but only if the game is accessible.
Rugby.body:
Money has always been a slightly dirty word in rugby. It was the original reason union and league went their separate ways back in 1895. It took union another 100 years to finally admit players deserved to be paid for their time. It was 90 years behind football in that respect, as highlighted by an excerpt from the following piece written by ex-Ireland international Andrew Trimble and Dan McKeown.

“Football made its peace with money in 1885, when the FA legalised professionalism in England rather than lose the northern clubs that were already paying players. Football has been learning how to run a professional sport for 140 years, rugby has been learning for 30. The governance philosophy in rugby union was designed for the amateur century, and is now being asked to do a job it was explicitly built to prevent.”

Rugby.title: Scotland name 32-player squad for two-match Australia tour
Rugby.summary: Interim head coach Dave Butcher has named the 32-player Scotland squad that will travel to Australia to play the Wallaroos in two Tests.
Rugby.body:
Interim head coach Dave Butcher has named the 32-player Scotland squad that will travel to Australia to play the Wallaroos in two Tests. In October, Scotland did not win in any of the three Test matches that they played. Heavy losses to Canada and the Black Ferns were followed by a 30-10 loss to Australia in Edinburgh, with Scotland hoping they can turn the tide in their three-match series in the Wallaroos.

The squad does not contain Emma Wassell and Alex Stewart, who sustained campaign ending injuries. There is a place for Rachel Philipps who has returned after going through concussion protocols.

Rugby.title: PWR lock in Final venue through 2029 in bid to ‘build something special’
Rugby.summary: JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby have confirmed that The Stoop will host the competition's showpiece finale in 2027, 2028 and 2029.
Rugby.body:
JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby have confirmed that The Stoop will host the competition’s showpiece final in 2027, 2028 and 2029. The home of Harlequins welcomed more than 8,000 supporters at the conclusion of the 2025/26 season, when Saracens ended their four-year wait for an English league title with a 52-14 victory over Trailfinders Women.

The West London venue, which sits across the road from Allianz Stadium, will now become the long-term host for the PWR Final as the league aims to establish an annual flagship event for supporters.

Rugby.summary: Marlie Packer will not travel with the Red Roses to North America for the latter half of WXV Global Series to ahead of the birth of her first child with Rosie Galligan.
Rugby.body:
Marlie Packer will not travel with the Red Roses to North America for the latter half of the WXV Global Series ahead of the birth of her first child with Rosie Galligan. The 37-year-old flanker, who has won 119 Test caps, played in all three of England’s home fixtures in September and started in the team’s win against the Black Ferns at Allianz Stadium.

Of the 32 players selected by John Mitchell for the tour, 24 played in fixtures against Australia, Canada and New Zealand. The squad does not include Delaney Burns, Haidee Head and Sophie McQueen, who have all been ruled out with injury.

Rugby.title: England forward Packer to miss North America tour
Rugby.summary: Two-time World Cup winner Marlie Packer will not travel with England to North America this month for Tests against Canada and the United States.
Rugby.body:
Two-time World Cup winner Marlie Packer will not travel with England to North America this month for Tests against Canada and the United States. The Harlequins back-rower will remain in the United Kingdom with her partner and Red Roses team-mate Rosie Galligan due to give birth.

England face Canada on 17 and 24 October (both 00:00 BST starts) before playing the USA in one-off match on 30 October (21:15 BST). England are boosted by the return of Kelsey Clifford for the North American tour, with the Saracens prop returning from a hamstring injury.

Rugby.title: Springboks great Francois Steyn set to call Swansea home
Rugby.summary: The Toyota Cheetahs will make Ospreys’ St Helen’s their European home this season after striking an agreement to stage their EPCR Challenge Cup pool fixtures in Swansea.
Rugby.body:
The Toyota Cheetahs will make Ospreys’ St Helen’s their European home this season after striking an agreement to stage their EPCR Challenge Cup pool fixtures in Swansea. The South African side, coached by Springboks great Francois Steyn, will face Dragons at the ground on December 13 before returning to take on Top 14 outfit Perpignan on January 17.

Both matches will form part of double-header weekends at St Helen’s. The Ospreys host Harlequins 24 hours before the Cheetahs meet the Dragons, while Vannes visit Swansea the day before the Cheetahs face Perpignan.

Rugby.title: Cheetahs to play European games in Swansea
Rugby.summary: South African side Cheetahs will play their European Challenge Cup home matches this season at St Helen's in Swansea, the home of Welsh side Ospreys.
Rugby.body:
South African side Cheetahs will play their European Challenge Cup home matches this season at St Helen's in Swansea, the home of Welsh side Ospreys. Cheetahs host Dragons on Sunday, 13 December and Perpignan on Sunday, 17 January with both games a day after Ospreys' home matches in the same competition.

Cheetahs have traditionally used Europe as a base for matches in the second-tier tournament, with games in the 2025-26 season taking place in Amsterdam. There are links between Ospreys and Cheetahs. Y11 Sports & Media owns a majority stake in the Ospreys and maintain an investment interest in the South African team with players moving between both sides.

Pierre Mignoni has stepped down from his role as Toulon head coach with immediate effect following a poor start to the Top 14 season which sees the side languishing in 13th place.

Rugby.title: Sudamérica Rugby gives Rugby World Cup 2035 bid update
Rugby.summary: South America's top rugby-playing countries, led by Argentina, have released a statement saying they have officially submitted all the information required by World Rugby to be considered as a candidate to host Rugby World Cup 2035.
Rugby.body:
South America’s top rugby-playing countries, led by Argentina, have released a statement saying they have officially submitted all the information required by World Rugby to be considered as a candidate to host Rugby World Cup 2035.

World Rugby launched the selection process for RWC 2035 at their General Assembly in London just over 12 months ago, and several countries have stepped forward. The preliminary hosting bid process includes the submission of documentation, visits to the candidate venues, and the announcement of the preferred venues in May 2027. The final decision will be made by the World Rugby Council in November 2027

Rugby.title: Quins display one of worst I have ever seen
Rugby.summary: Ugo Monye calls former club Harlequins' 48-0 defeat by Gloucester "one of the worst performances I have ever seen".
Rugby.body:
Former Harlequins winger Ugo Monye has called the club's 48-0 defeat by Gloucester on Saturday "one of the worst performances I have ever seen". Quins conceded eight tries in their heaviest league defeat for 26 years and are bottom of the early Gallagher Prem table.

"They got smashed in the scrum and the line-out. Their backfield coverage was poor. They got smashed at the gain line," Monye said on the Rugby Union Weekly podcast. "They didn't score a single point in a league where they're literally handing out points for free [this season]."

Rugby.title: Tana Umaga: 'You can definitely see the stamp of Les Kiss on this Wallabies side'
Rugby.summary: The changes Kiss has made have borne fruit, and All Blacks defence coach Tana Umaga was quick to put his finger on exactly where they've come when speaking with media after training on Tuesday.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks are looking forward to facing a familiar foe with a similar attacking mindset when the Bledisloe Cup kicks off in Auckland this weekend, but their rivals from across the ditch have some new quirks to their game that demand defensive adjustments.

The Kiwis aren’t the only side introducing a new head coach’s game plan this year, with Les Kiss the new kid on the Wallabies’ block. Wins over Japan, Argentina and South Africa have got Kiss’ tenure off to a flying start just one year out from a home Rugby World Cup, and there would be no better way to affirm that momentum than not only ending a more than two-decade-long Bledisloe Cup drought, but also New Zealand’s three-decade-long unbeaten run at Eden Park.

Rugby.title: ‘Sticks in the guts’: Tana Umaga on defensive response required against Wallabies
Rugby.summary: "It's probably the one stat we look at the most: the three in the red that we lost," the former Moana Pasifika head coach said in Auckland on Tuesday.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks defence coach and former captain Tana Umaga has urged his side to bounce back against the Wallabies at Eden Park, after slumping to three straight defeats against the Springboks.

Umaga, who was appointed by All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie as the team’s defence coach, admitted in Auckland on Tuesday that he’s not sure an All Blacks side in his lifetime has ever lost three Tests on the trot while conceding an average of 35 points.

Rugby.summary: Toe sii e Malisi le ipu o le siamupini o le Taula Marist Rugby Sevens Festival III 2026 Radio Samoa
Rugby.body:
A’o toe sauni ‘au lakapi mai kalapu ‘ese’ese i le atunuu i le vae lona 2 o le ta’amilosaga lakapi taito’afitu a le Vodafone i le Aso Faraile ma le Aso To’ona’i o le vaiaso fou, ua mae’a le ta’amilosaga taito’afitu a le Taula Marist Rugby Sevens i le faaiuga o le vaiaso ua mavae ma ua manumalo ai i le ipu a Leituala Joseph Chan Ting Memorial Cup le ‘au a le Malisi lea na o la iloilo ai ma le ‘au o le Kofeula mai Satapuala le siamupini o le ta’amilosaga.

O isi vaega poo division o lea lava ta’amilosaga lakapi taito’afitu ua siamupini ai le ‘au e i lalo o le 18 tausaga poo le under 18 o le Kokonut Production Tama Uli, Under 18 a tama’ita’i ua siamupini ai le Savai’i Queen, Under 16 a ali’i ua sola ma le ‘au a ali’i o le Savai’i sonic le siamupini, o le ‘au a ali’i a le Malisi ua siamupini i le vaega o le Under 14, ae siamupini le ‘au a tama’ita’i o le No Idea Development –Flash i le vaega o ‘au feiloi poo mix i le matutua e i lalo o le 10 tausaga poo le under 10.

Rugby.title: ‘Australia are hitting a sweet spot of Test experience; it’s exciting to think where they could get to over the next 12 months’
Rugby.summary: With RWC 2027 just under a year away, Australia fans are daring to dream about what sort of shape their team might be in by then.
Rugby.body:
There’s a train of thought among rugby aficionados, commentators and pundits, that somewhere in the vicinity of 25 to 40 Tests of experience represents something of a sweet spot for players building their international careers.

The thinking is that once inside this range, players know more about the requirements of the top level of the game and how they need to prepare for it, they’re probably less inclined to make the kind of errors under pressure or fatigue that might easily be put down to inexperience, and they’re no longer a risky decision at the selection table.

Rugby.title: Saracens management letting players down
Rugby.summary: Former England scrum-half Danny Care says "some of the powers that be" at Saracens have "let the players down".
Rugby.body:
Former England scrum-half Danny Care says "some of the powers that be" at Saracens have "let the players down" after a turbulent start to the season. An opening weekend 40-38 win at Leicester was followed by a 21-17 home defeat by Sale, the build-up to which was marred by headlines made by returning director of rugby Brendan Venter.

He reportedly refused to perform a series of media obligations, putting Saracens at risk of fines amid conjecture his job title had been changed to 'head of rugby culture and wine consultant', although the club have since clarified he is now head of culture and technical director.

Rugby.summary: Ugo, Ashy and Danny raise a glass and dissect round two of the Prem season.
Rugby.body: Ugo, Ashy and Danny raise a glass to Brendan Venter’s short stint as Saracens’ wine consultant and review round two of the Prem. Rugby.title: 'Gloucester deserves a top rugby team playing at the top of the league'
Rugby.summary: Winless after their first two games last season, and sat eighth in the table, Gloucester have flipped the script this term and breezed past Exeter 45-24 and Harlequins 48-0.
Rugby.body:
After two bonus point wins from two, Gloucester are sitting pretty at the top of the Gallagher PREM table, ahead of West Country rivals Bristol and Bath on points difference. It may be early days, but the turnaround at Kingsholm is quickly becoming one of the early storylines of the season.

Winless after their first two games last season, and sat eighth in the table, Gloucester have flipped the script this term and breezed past Exeter 45-24 and Harlequins 48-0. It is the first time since the start of the 2007/08 season, the year they finished the regular season in first place but lost in the semi-finals of the playoffs to an Andy Goode drop goal, that the Cherry & Whites have looked down on the rest of the PREM two matches in.

Rugby.summary: He scored a brace of tries in last Friday’s 47-27 bonus point victory over Zebre Parma at the Arms Park, taking his tally to 13 from 21 appearances in all competitions for the club.

Try machine Tom Bowen has a simple message for all smaller players in the game: “Back yourself”. At 5ft 7ins and 11st 11lbs, the Cardiff Rugby winger is dwarfed by some of the giants on the circuit, but he is standing tall with his performances.

Rugby.title: Big Ireland win sees Wales benefit in World Rugby rankings
Rugby.summary: Ireland's 43-19 victory over Japan in Cork has seen Wales return to 11th in the World Rugby rankings.
Rugby.body:
Ireland’s 43-19 victory over Japan in Cork has seen Wales return to 11th in the World Rugby rankings. On Saturday afternoon, Eilis Cahill, Brittany Hogan, Neve Jones, Anna McGann, Beibhinn Parsons, Alana McInerney and Sophie Barrett all crossed the whitewash at Virgin Media Park to rack up an impressive win.

The victory means that Ireland have now won two of their three fixtures so far this autumn. Their most recent fixture against Japan took place out of the WXV Global Series window, just one week after they beat the Sakura Fifteen 31-24 in Galway.

Rugby.summary: The Springbok Women ended their European tour on Sunday with a 20-0 win over Spain in Seville.
Rugby.body:
The Springbok Women ended their European tour on Sunday with a 20-0 win over Spain in Seville. A WXV Global Series crossover fixture against Regis Sonnes’ Las Leonas, who finished third in the 2026 WXV Global Series Challenger, saw South Africa claim their second win of the tour.

In Seville, Catha Jacobs finished off a sensational scrum move to open the scoring after 14 minutes. Jakkie Cilliers converted the try before adding three more points from the tee in the 30th minute to give the visitors a 10-0 half-time lead.

Rugby.summary: Nel Metcalfe is in a 30-strong party that will be led by co-captains Alex Callender and Kate Williams for back-to-back Tests in Japan.
Rugby.body:
Full-back Nel Metcalfe has a chance to resurrect her Wales career after being named in Sean Lynn's squad for their WXV double-header against Japan. The 21-year-old Gloucester-Hartpury player has fully recovered from the knee injury that ruled her out of the 2026 Women's Six Nations.

Lynn named Metcalfe in his extended training squad for the stunning WXV win against South Africa and subsequent defeat by the United States, but she did not make the matchday squads.

Rugby.summary: Scott Bemand believed that Ireland left points out on the pitch after their 43-19 win against Japan on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Ireland head coach Scott Bemand believes his side could have scored 50 or even 60 points against Japan despite their 43-19 victory in Cork on Saturday. The out-of-window Test at Virgin Media Park saw Ireland run in seven tries, although Japan threatened a comeback in the second half before the hosts pulled away late on.

The Sakura Fifteen took an early lead when Sakurako Korai bundled over in the fourth minute, but Ireland responded with four tries in the following 36 minutes from Eilis Cahill, Brittany Hogan, Neve Jones and Anna McGann.

Rugby.title: Salty celebrations, questionable signings and Test bolters
Rugby.summary: Bristol set out their top-four aspirations with a statement win, while Gloucester's renaissance continues in the second round of Prem action.
Rugby.body:
The stats piled up after a car-crash performance by Harlequins in a 48-0 shellacking by Gloucester. The biggest league defeat in 26 years. Seventeen penalties conceded. Only two entries made into the opposition 22m. Not one of their starting forward pack making more than four carries.

It was a desperately under-powered display. Boss Jason Gilmore described it as "totally unacceptable" in the aftermath. The Australian has overseen a few eyesores during his time in charge; a 38-0 reverse at Sandy Park and a 40-14 reverse at the club's festive fixture at Allianz Stadium come to mind.

Rugby.summary: Wales boss Sean Lynn has named a 30-player squad to tour Japan in October as part of WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
Wales boss Sean Lynn has named a 30-player squad to tour Japan in October as part of WXV Global Series. Nel Metcalfe, who missed the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations with injury, has returned to the squad. The Gloucester Hartpury full-back has not turned out for Wales since the team’s loss to Fiji at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025.

The squad will continue to be co-captained by back-row pair Alex Callender and Kate Williams. Uncapped prop forwards Stella Orrin and Crystal James have been named in the squad.

Rugby.title: Golden Finish in Nagoya for Hong Kong China Men and Japan Women
Rugby.summary: Golden Finish in Nagoya for Hong Kong China Men and Japan Women asiarugby.com
Rugby.body:
Hong Kong China claimed the men’s gold medal and Japan secured the women’s title as rugby sevens at the Aichi–Nagoya 2026 Asian Games concluded in front of a capacity crowd at Nagoya City Mizuho Park Rugby Field on Saturday, 3 October.

Hong Kong China defeated China in the men’s final to secure their third consecutive Asian Games gold medal, following titles in Jakarta in 2018 and Hangzhou in 2023. Hong Kong China reached the final by defeating Korea, while China edged hosts Japan in a closely contested semi-final. Japan recovered to claim the men’s bronze medal, completing the podium alongside Hong Kong China and China.

Rugby.title: 'I could skip homework if I went to rugby training': Marius Simionescu, the reluctant player who became Romania's kingpin
Rugby.summary: Rugby bored the full-back as a teenager, but he was persuaded to stick at the game, and now a key man for Romania, cannot imagine life without it.
Rugby.body:
Goosebumps. There’s no other way to describe listening to Marius Simionescu, a beacon of the Romania team, map out his rugby journey. The full-back talks with burning passion about what the game has given him, as he left home and familiarity behind to chase his dreams and represent his country.

The 29-year-old was born in the town of Erbiceni and raised mostly in Ia?i, a region in the far eastern corner of Romania. His parents moved to Italy to earn a better living for their family and Simionescu spent much of his childhood under the care of his grandmother. He was 14 when rugby found him, persuaded by renowned Romanian coach Gabriel Popa to join a local team.

Rugby.summary: The Hollywoodbets Sharks are the early pacesetters in the BKT URC as the only team with maximum points after the opening two rounds of matches.
Rugby.body:
The Hollywoodbets Sharks are the early pacesetters in the BKT URC as the only team with maximum points after the opening two rounds of matches. The Durban-based side missed out on the play-offs last term, but they clearly mean business this time time around.

They recorded a second successive bonus point victory by beating defending champions Leinster Rugby 26-20 at Kings Park on Saturday evening. The Player of the Match award went to their winger Edwill van der Merwe who secured both the win and a bonus with a try two minutes from time.

Rugby.title: Former England back-row scores in Top 14 ahead of potential debut for new nation
Rugby.summary: Former England No.8 Nathan Hughes capped his call-up to Fiji’s squad by bagging a try in his first appearance of the Top 14 season for Racing 92 on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Former England No.8 Nathan Hughes capped his call-up to Fiji’s squad by bagging a try in his first appearance of the Top 14 season for Racing 92 on Saturday. The 35-year-old came off the bench in Racing’s 55-25 victory over Perpignan, making an immediate impact just days after being included in the Flying Fijians’ 68-man extended squad.

Hughes, who won 22 caps for England between 2016 and 2019, missed out on Fiji’s Nations Championship squad in July but is now back in the frame ahead of the Test against Japan on October 24 and the Nations Championship fixtures that follow.

Rugby.summary: Blackheath FC's 33-26 victory over Doncaster Knights in the Elior Champ was their first at Level 2 in the English league system since 1 May, 1999.
Rugby.body:
After two near-misses, Blackheath FC celebrated their first win at Level 2 in the English league system for 27 years when they beat Doncaster Knights 33-26 in the Elior Champ at The Utilita, Well Hall on Sunday.

Blackheath, the oldest rugby club in the world, had picked up losing bonus points in their first two Champ games, after falling just short against Nottingham (31-38) and Caldy (24-28) on the opening two weekends.

Rugby.title: Allan Alaalatoa explains Wallabies’ ‘main focus’ before Bledisloe Cup opener
Rugby.summary: Allan Alaalatoa believes the visitors can take confidence and belief from their preparation into the fixture.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies are under no illusions about the challenge that awaits at the All Blacks’ Eden Park fortress this weekend, but Allan Alaalatoa believes the visitors can take confidence and belief from their preparation into the fixture.

Alaalatoa made his 39th appearance in the gold jersey when the Wallabies last defeated the All Blacks on November 7, 2020. The now 94-Test prop remains a regular starter for the Wallabies, who come into the Bledisloe Cup series on a six-game unbeaten run.

Rugby.title: The biggest handbrake on the Wallabies’ momentum ahead of their Bledisloe Cup bid
Rugby.summary: On the surface, the Wallabies seem to have all the right cards to enter the Bledisloe Cup race with confidence and momentum, but the closing of the Regulation 9 window, injuries, and suspensions will mean the bad type of selection headaches for Kiss and his assistants.
Rugby.body:
Rugby Regulation 9 window is now closed. Regulation 9, which provides official release windows for overseas players to return to their national sides, is not in effect for the Bledisloe Cup series in October, and it means the Wallabies are without two of their best and most impactful forwards, Taniela Tupou and Tom Hooper, for the two toughest matches of 2026.

There’s no two ways about it: the Tests against the second-best team in the world, the All Blacks, are the two hardest matches the Wallabies will play all year. Not only will the All Blacks be desperate to retain the Bledisloe Cup after a disappointing Greatest Rivalry Tour, but they won’t be fielding a heavily rotated side as the Boks did in Perth.

Rugby.summary: Billionaire Roosters boss teases big signing after two grand final wins Nine.com.au
Rugby.body:
A cross-code star is set to make her way to the Sydney Roosters NRLW team next year, in a move that is only going to make the premiership winners even stronger. Rugby.title: Sale Sharks player ratings vs Saracens | 2026/27 Gallagher PREM
Rugby.summary: Eight days removed from a frustrating home loss to open the season, Alex Sanderson's Sale Sharks pulled off the rarest of away wins at the Stone-X to down Saracens 21 - 17.
Rugby.body:
Eight days removed from a frustrating home loss to open the season, Alex Sanderson’s Sale Sharks pulled off the rarest of away wins at the Stone-X to down Saracens 21 – 17. Built on a foundation of defensive belligerence, the Sharks led by Tom Curry, Joe Marchant and Courtney Lawes battered the Saracens attack. Stunting any really opportunities to get flow into their attack, the Sharks overcame a two man deficit to limit Saracens to just five points at half-time.

Coming out of the blocks quickly in the second half through a moment of magic by Tom O’Flaherty, the visitors had their tails up. A try by Sione Va’enuku brought the home side back to within a score three minutes later but as had been the case all afternoon, Sanderson’s side responded through Ben Bamber in the 65th minute.

Rugby.title: Sale defy Jacques Vermeulen’s first-half red card to beat Saracens
Rugby.summary: Sale defied Jacques Vermeulen’s first-half red card to dispatch Saracens 21-17 with Tom O’Flaherty emerging as the star of a slug fest at StoneX Stadium.
Rugby.body:
Sale defied Jacques Vermeulen’s first-half red card to dispatch Saracens 21-17 with Tom O’Flaherty emerging as the star of a slug fest at StoneX Stadium. Vermeulen was shown a 20-minute red for a dangerous tackle on Tomos Williams at a point in the first half when Alex Lozowski was in the sin bin because of the same offence.

Saracens then took control but it was only temporary and in the 41st minute O’Flaherty produced the match’s pivotal moment by racing over for a dynamic solo try. It was part of a dominant second half from Sale, who capitalised on the hosts’ lifeless performance to bounce back after losing to Bristol on the opening weekend with their hooker Nathan Jibulu also outstanding.

Sale overcame Jacques Vermeulen's red card to defeat Saracens and pick up their first win of The Prem campaign. Sarries struggled to break down a stubborn Sharks defence despite having numerical superiority for 27 minutes of the first half after Alex Lozowski's yellow and Vermeulen's 20-minute red card.

Incredibly, Sale took a 7-5 lead into half-time thanks to Nathan Jibulu's early converted try, despite Eroni Mawi's reply, and then went further ahead soon after the break as Tom O'Flaherty raced in.

Rugby.title: History made in Top 14 as longstanding record falls to Pumas fly-half
Rugby.summary: Twice retired 40-year-old Pumas fly-half Benjamín Urdapilleta made Top 14 history on Saturday after nailing his second of three kicks in USA Perpignan's match against Racing 92.
Rugby.body:
Twice retired 40-year-old Pumas fly-half Benjamín Urdapilleta made Top 14 history on Saturday after nailing his second of three kicks in USA Perpignan’s match against Racing 92.

Heading into the match, the former Pumas international had recorded 2,611 points in the Top 14, just a couple behind Romain Teulet in the professional era. The fly-half then matched Teulet’s record after converting Braydon Ennor’s try, then added two more successful penalty kicks, setting the new record at 2,619.

With 66 points, 10 tries, five yellow cards and some late chaos, the 33-33 draw between Glasgow and Ulster is an early contender for one of the games of the United Rugby Championship season.

Rugby.title: 'A great sign'
Rugby.summary: Leicester head coach Geoff Parling believes there is still “loads to improve on” following their 24-19 win over Newcastle at Kingston Park.
Rugby.body:
Leicester head coach Geoff Parling believes there is still “loads to improve on” following their 24-19 win over Newcastle at Kingston Park. The hosts went ahead through Obi Ene, but Leicester regained control and claimed a 17-5 lead at the break as Samiuela Moli and Adam Radwan both crossed and Billy Searle kicked a penalty.

A closely-fought second half saw George McGuigan score for Newcastle before Will Hurd charged over from a close-range tap and go to extend the Tigers’ advantage. However, the visitors were forced to hang on toward the end as Cam Jordan went over and Parling revealed there were mixed feelings in the changing room post-match.

Rugby.title: Oliver Smith's double helps Australia U18 rally to beat NZ Schools in thriller
Rugby.summary: Both sides attacked ferociously in the opening stages, but it was New Zealand that were offered the first real opportunity of the contest.
Rugby.body:
Australia U18 have come up clutch against New Zealand Schools, beating the hosts 40-33 at St Paul’s Collegiate in Hamilton, in an end-to-end battle. Dale Roberson’s side, clearly the most impressive team at the tournament, came from behind to overpower the Kiwis in Hamilton. Despite the home side leading 19-12 at the break, Australia burst out of the blocks after halftime to stun New Zealand Schools on Sunday evening.

The first half was a thrilling contest filled with lead changes and big moments, with both sets of captains coming up with huge plays on both sides of the ball. The home side, coached by New Zealand Pathways coach Kane Jury, looked the more threatening with ball in hand, but the Australian defence held strong on several occasions.

Rugby.title: Trying to style Henry Pollock into a rugby icon is missing something
Rugby.summary: This Pollock stuff is about Pollock. It’s not about Northampton or England. It’s not even about rugby. It’s about a promoter deciding, seemingly on a whim, that this is a person of substance that we’re going to be told is transformational so many times.
Rugby.body:
If this is where rugby is going, it might be a journey it takes without me. Rugby, to me, is the ultimate team game. Tall or short, big or small, there’s always been a place for you.

It’s not about individuals, but the collective. If you’re modest, hardworking and brave you’ll earn the respect of everyone. No-one’s bigger than the team, no-one says or does stupid things that put a target on people’s heads. You talk a small game, but play a big one.

Rugby.title: The URC talking points as Wales hopefuls impress
Rugby.summary: Which players are impressing as Cardiff and Dragons enjoy strong starts in the United Rugby Championship while Scarlets and Ospreys are still hunting a win.
Rugby.body:
Only two rounds of the United Rugby Championship (URC) have been completed but it is Cardiff and Dragons who are the early Welsh pacesetters, while Scarlets and Ospreys are languishing at the bottom of the table in 14th and 15th respectively.

Cardiff have won both games and lie second, while Dragons in sixth are unbeaten after winning an entertaining 10-try derby against Scarlets in Newport. Ospreys and Scarlets are battling for long-term survival, with only one west Wales side set to exist in two years, but currently they would love just a victory after two defeats each.

Rugby.summary: "So generally, when the kicks are a little bit deeper, it allows you to then feed the fullback or ten, and then we get to play immediately, try and move the ball away from that congested area."
Rugby.body:
After weeks of discussing, reviewing, and “kicking stones” about their 3-1 series defeat against the Springboks in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie is ready to make amends.

Rennie’s side tried to implement a new aerial strategy during the four-Test, eight-game tour of the Republic, where the wingers, or any player, for that matter, attempting to secure an in-play kick, would retreat instead of attacking the ball from front on.

Rugby.summary: The Tigers managed to see the game out to move into fifth after two Prem matches, while Newcastle slipped to a second successive league defeat.
Rugby.body:
Leicester clinched their first Gallagher Prem win of the season with a 24-19 victory over Newcastle. Making his Newcastle bow in front of a sold-out Kingston Park, Obi Ene crossed early on, but the Tigers soon took control as tries from Samiuela Moli and Adam Radwan along with a Billy Searle penalty handed them a 17-5 lead at the break.

George McGuigan went over in the second half for Newcastle, but Will Hurd’s try extended Leicester’s advantage and they withstood a late scare when Cam Jordan crossed for the hosts in the last 10 minutes.

Former Newcastle winger Adam Radwan scored on his return to Kingston Park as the Tigers won for the first time in seven matches in all competitions, following a dismal run which stretches back into last season.

After being edged out by two points in a high-scoring thriller by Saracens six days ago, Leicester had to show their grit and determination to cling on to victory against a Newcastle side who threatened a late comeback.

Rugby.title: Dowson praises ‘exceptional’ England hopeful after frustrating champions
Rugby.summary: Bristol boss Pat Lam hailed Louis Rees-Zammit’s “lethal” quality after he inspired the Bears’ 41-26 victory over Gallagher Prem champions Northampton at Ashton Gate.
Rugby.body:
Bristol boss Pat Lam hailed Louis Rees-Zammit’s “lethal” quality after he inspired the Bears’ 41-26 victory over Gallagher Prem champions Northampton at Ashton Gate. The Wales wing followed up his two tries against opening Prem opponents Sale Sharks with another double as Bristol triumphed in bonus-point fashion.

“He is sharp, you know, and he loves finishing,” Lam said. “We know that if we can give him time and space, he is lethal. He is back on the wing (Rees-Zammit made appearances at full-back for club and country last season), and most importantly that is where he wants to be.”

Rugby.body:
Gloucester continued their impressive start to the Gallagher Prem season by handing out a 48-0 thrashing to hapless Harlequins at Kingsholm. The eight-try win followed up their impressive opening day victory over Exeter at Sandy Park – but that success was far more meritorious as Harlequins were incredibly poor on the day.

Quins were outplayed in every aspect of the game and never looked like opening their tally. They were without a few leading players including England internationals, Marcus Smith and Alex Dombrandt, but it will take time for them to recover from this.

Quins were outplayed in every aspect of the game and never looked like opening their tally. They were without a few leading players including England internationals, Marcus Smith and Alex Dombrandt, but it will take time for them to recover from this.

Rugby.title: Glasgow and Ulster play out thrilling draw in URC
Rugby.summary: George Horne's late penalty hits the post as Glasgow Warriors and Ulster play out a thrilling 33-33 draw in the United Rugby Championship.
Rugby.body:
George Horne's late penalty hit the post as Glasgow Warriors and Ulster played out a thrilling 33-33 draw in the United Rugby Championship. Ulster, seeking their first win in Glasgow in more than five years, led 19-14 at the break but the Warriors scored three tries in a clinical nine-minute spell when Ulster had two players sin-binned to take the lead.

But Glasgow were reduced to 13 inside the final 10 minutes and Juarno Augustus' try, converted by Nathan Doak, levelled the game. Despite being two players down, Horne had a chance to win the match but his penalty came back off the upright with four minutes left and the points were shared at Scotstoun.

Rugby.body:
Ireland scored seven tries as they secured a comprehensive 43-19 win over Japan in their Test match at Virgin Media Park in Cork on Saturday. Scott Bemand's side had defeated the same opponents in a WXV Global Series encounter in Galway the previous weekend.

Ireland recovered from conceding an early try to cross the whitewash four times in the first half to help them to a 22-7 advantage at the break. Japan rallied but the hosts extended their lead in the second period to ensure they travel to face South Africa for a two-match series in the WXV with confidence high and momentum gathered.

Rugby.body:
Exeter boss Rob Baxter has urged Henry Slade not to dwell on his missed kicks in their loss at Bath. Slade missed two first-half conversions before hitting the post with a penalty late in the second half as Chiefs went down 40-34 in a thrilling game at the Rec.

Team-mate Harvey Skinner stepped up to kick a 79th-minute penalty for Exeter that secured a losing bonus point as Baxter's side search for a first win of the season. "I think we've been very fortunate with Henry over the years, but particularly last year," Baxter told BBC Radio Devon as Slade practised kicks after the final whistle.

Mark Jones' Ospreys started the 2026-27 season by claiming a four-try bonus point in defeat by Sharks in Durban, but they left Johannesburg without anything to show for their efforts on Saturday.

Rugby.title: HK men’s Rugby Sevens claim historic hat-trick of Asian Games titles with shutout victory
Rugby.summary: HK men’s Rugby Sevens claim historic hat-trick of Asian Games titles with shutout victory thestandard.com.hk
Rugby.body:
Hong Kong’s men’s rugby sevens team has written a glorious new chapter in the city's sporting history by successfully defending their Asian Games gold medal in Nagoya, defeating the national team with a commanding 26-0 shutout.

This triumphant victory secures an unprecedented third consecutive Asian Games crown for the squad, while simultaneously elevating Hong Kong's gold medal haul at these Games to an all-time high of 11. The historic gold also takes the city's overall medal tally to 54, officially breaking the previous record set at the Hangzhou Games.

Rugby.title: Asian Games: city’s men make it hat-trick of rugby sevens golds, women win bronze
Rugby.summary: Asian Games: city’s men make it hat-trick of rugby sevens golds, women win bronze South China Morning Post
Rugby.body:
There are very few certainties in life, although Hong Kong’s men winning rugby sevens gold at the Asian Games could well be one of them. A 26-0 win over China on Saturday sealed a third consecutive title for the city’s team at the Games, and it is now 12 years since they last lost a match at the multi-sport event.

Their mainland opponents had already been beaten 22-0 in a Pool A game on Friday, and a first-half double from Harry Sayers ended any threat of an upset. Bryn Phillips added a third, and converted all three as well, ensuring there was no way back for China. With little need to press the issue in the second half, the only additional score came seconds after the restart, with Juan Esono Mba Oyana crossing in the corner.

Rugby.summary: 363 days on from the heartbreak of a narrow defeat in the inaugural Super Rugby AUS Grand Final, the Western Force have gone one better.
Rugby.body:
363 days on from the heartbreak of a narrow defeat in the inaugural Super Rugby AUS Grand Final, the Western Force have gone one better by overcoming defending champions the NSW Waratahs 53-26 at Perth’s Scotch College.

Winger Dylan Pietsch, 95-Test Wallaby Kurtley Beale and Australia Sevens representative Wallace Charlie all impressed as the Force ran away with an emphatic result. It’s a drought-breaking title for the Force, with the men’s team last claiming silverware in the 2019 Global Rapid Rugby and National Rugby Championship. The Force made the playoffs two years later in Super Rugby AU but the wait for another title went on.

Rugby.summary: Bulls lock Reinhardt Ludwig is starting to attract serious interest from Japan Rugby League One outfits despite being tied down at Loftus Versfeld until the summer of 2028.
Rugby.body:
Bulls lock Reinhardt Ludwig is starting to attract serious interest from Japan Rugby League One outfits despite being tied down at Loftus Versfeld until the summer of 2028. Ludwig, 24, who also plays at blindside flanker, made his Bulls debut in a defeat against the Stormers in January 2021 and started the new season on fire, scoring two tries and winning 10 lineouts in the win in Zebre.

Japanese clubs are taking a close look at the former Baby Bok, a Junior World Cup winner five years ago, who has forced his way back into Johan Ackermann’s plans after seven months in the wilderness following Ruan Nortje’s departure.

Rugby.summary: Former Maori All Blacks captain Kurt Eklund has announced his sudden retirement from rugby due to a neck injury.
Rugby.body:
Former Maori All Blacks captain Kurt Eklund has announced his sudden retirement from rugby due to a neck injury. The 82-cap Blues hooker, who hasn’t featured on the field since round 14 of the Super Rugby Pacific season, made the announcement ahead of Bay of Plenty’s final game of the NPC round-robin.

Eklund, 34, was a key figure in the Blues’ all-conquering 2024 season, earning him an All Blacks XV call-up and further Maori All Blacks honours before he assumed captaincy of the latter team in 2025.

Both teams are hoping to repeat podium finishes from 2022. Hong Kong China’s men’s team are two-time defending gold medalists, while the women won the city’s first ever rugby sevens women’s medal with bronze in Hangzhou, China.

The men’s seven extended their unbeaten streak to five games without conceding a point to reach tomorrow’s semifinals against South Korea at 11.20. “Everything has gone to plan so far. That first game against China really was a challenge, and the boys responded quite well and were patient. It didn't happen in the first phase or second phase, like what we had in the previous games, so I thought we managed that game particularly well.

Rugby.body:
Bath made it two wins out of two in the new Prem season as they gained a degree of revenge for losing to Exeter Chiefs in last season's semi-final. The two sides produced another thrilling game, just as they did three months ago, exchanging 11 tries as the all-out attack approach to the new season continued.

The hosts scored four tries to have a bonus point in the bag by the break as Cameron Redpath, Bernard van der Linde, Dan du Preez and Finn Russell all scored to put them 26-10 ahead.

Rugby.summary: Debutant Ciaran Frawley’s 77th-minute try helped Connacht open their account in the new United Rugby Championship with a 22-19 victory at Benetton.
Rugby.body:
Debutant Ciaran Frawley’s 77th-minute try helped Connacht open their account in the new United Rugby Championship with a 22-19 victory at Benetton. After the Irish outfit lost at home to Stormers last weekend, Stuart Lancaster’s side were heading for another defeat with Benetton able to open up a narrow two-point lead thanks to Bautista Bernasconi’s score early in the second half.

However, Frawley followed up a fine first try for the club with a slick finish after an excellent team move to spark jubilant scenes in Italy after a last-gasp win. Only five minutes were on the clock in Treviso when Cian Prendergast put Connacht ahead, but it sparked a frantic opening 40.

Rugby.body:
Bath beat Exeter Chiefs 40-34 in a pulsating West Country derby at the Rec to take them to the top of the Gallagher Prem table but they were made to fight all the way in an 11-try thriller.

Cam Redpath, Dan du Preez, Bernard van der Linde, Ted Hill and Finn Russell scored Bath’s tries. There was also a penalty try award with Russell converting four.

The 25-year-old played the entire 80 minutes of the impressive 45-24 victory at Sandy Park but head coach George Skivington told BBC Radio Gloucestershire - before the extent of the injury was known - that he "caught his foot" towards the end of the game.

Cokanasiga joined the Cherry and Whites this summer from United Rugby Championship side Ospreys and scored two tries on his debut in the Prem Rugby Cup defeat by Bristol earlier this month.

Rugby.title: Saracens exile was 'bewildering', says returning Lozowski
Rugby.summary: Sale centre Alex Lozowski says the end of his decade-long stint at Saracens was an anti-climax after being reduced to a fringe player for his farewell campaign.
Rugby.body:
Sale centre Alex Lozowski says the end of his decade-long stint at Saracens was "sad" and "bewildering" after being reduced to a fringe player for his farewell campaign. The 33-year-old England international made only two Prem appearances for Saracens last season, with a 10-minute Champions Cup cameo off the bench his only game time since the end of February.

"It was a sad ending for everyone I suppose," said Lozowski. "They finished fifth, which is not where they wanted to be, and I wasn't part of it at all. "It was probably just a bit of a damp squib at the end of the season really, which was a shame. It was bewildering and peculiar to me.

Rugby.title: Injured stars hope for Christmas miracles as URC rivals smell Irish blood in the water
Rugby.summary: With two key Ireland players on the sidelines and all four provinces losing their opening URC games, the league's most dominant country is on the back foot.
Rugby.body:
As World Rugby marked a one-year countdown to Australia hosting the 2027 World Cup, a host of Ireland stars were named in their first squads of the season. Sam Prendergast, Ciarán Frawley, Craig Casey, Robbie Henshaw, Cormac Izuchukwu, Tom Clarkson, Cian Prendergast and Rónan Kelleher will launch into their seasons this weekend. There will be highs, lows, injuries, axings, accolades, analysis sessions, dropped balls and stuffed mauls in between, but all will hope to do enough to make it to the start line Down Under next year.

Two players decidedly out of the spotlight for a significant chunk of those 12 months are key to Ireland’s World Cup cause. Leinster and Ireland captain Caelan Doris will not return until early 2027. The 28-year-old broke his foot at the tail-end of last season – missing summer Test matches for the second year running. Doris had surgery on that busted foot over the summer, and also had a procedure carried out on his knee. There have been complications with his rehabilitation timeline, according to The Irish Times, caused by an infection picked up in that repaired knee. Leinster are sharing around the captaincy until he returns, with Dan Sheehan likeliest to lead Ireland when the Nations Championship re-opens for business in November.
