There have been complications with his rehabilitation timeline, according to The Irish Times, caused by an infection picked up in that repaired knee. Leinster are sharing around the captaincy until he returns, with Dan Sheehan likeliest to lead Ireland when the Nations Championship re-opens for business in November.

Rugby.title: 'Godfather of defence': Sharks ready for Leinster and the Jacques Nienaber effect
Rugby.summary: As the Sharks prepare to take on the Irish powerhouse Leinster this Saturday at Kings Park in the United Rugby Championship, attention will inevitably shift from the players on the field to the coaching staff.
Rugby.body:
As the Sharks gear up to face the formidable Leinster this Saturday at Kings Park during Round Two of the URC, the spotlight will inevitably shift from the athletes on the pitch to the strategic minds guiding them.

At the forefront is Leinster’s senior coach, Jacques Nienaber, who will find himself under keen scrutiny. Sharks’ defence coach, Joey Mongalo, has chosen to approach the idea of a personal rivalry with caution, referring to Nienaber as “the godfather of defence.”

Rugby.title: Wade closes in on record as tries dominate Prem
Rugby.summary: Christian Wade sits four away from Chris Ashton's all-time record of 101 as tries dominate Prem Rugby.
Rugby.body:
The opening week of the new Prem season was all about tries, tries, tries as the league's 10 teams went on all-out attack. No fewer than 52 tries were scored across the five matches, setting a record for the opening round of a season, with an average of more than 10 per game and four players claiming hat-tricks as spectators were royally entertained.

Contributing two of those scores was Christian Wade for Newcastle Red Bulls in their 59-26 loss at Northampton Saints, as the veteran winger moves closer to an all-time record.

Rugby.title: Report: Early TV viewing figures for PREM add to upbeat mood
Rugby.summary: Across four metered televised matches, the cumulative audience on TNT Sports was more than double that of 2025/26: over 795,000, compared with 390,000 last year.
Rugby.body:
TV viewing figures for round one of the new Gallagher PREM season are double what they were at this stage of the competition last year. Entertainment may mean different things to different people, but it seems armchair fans are buying into the high-scoring fare on offer. The 52 tries scored last weekend are a record for the opening round of the 30-season old competition, which for the last four seasons, has only involved 10 teams as opposed to anything between 11 and 14 in the past.

As reported by Andy Milnes of Neisen Sports, across four metered televised matches, the cumulative audience on TNT Sports was over 795,000, compared with 390,000 last year. Those numbers do not include non-metered coverage of Bath’s 33-17 win over between Harlequins on the opening night, which was carried on TNT Sports 5.

Rugby.summary: New Scarlets lock Alex Groves describes his remarkable return to rugby following heart surgery.
Rugby.body:
New Scarlets lock Alex Groves make his first league start on Saturday when he lines up against the Dragons in the United Rugby Championship (URC). The fact the 25-year-old is playing at all is remarkable considering he underwent major eight-hour heart surgery in February 2024.

There was not just a question whether he would play again. There was even concern about his survival. "I was confident as a young boy that I was fit and healthy and never thought anything was wrong with me. It was such a shock when I found out.

Rugby.title: 'After watching the Aussies on the weekend...': Richie Mo'unga's take on Wallabies
Rugby.summary: Richie Mo'unga is expecting to face a Wallabies team full of confidence when the All Blacks host their trans-Tasman rivals at Eden Park next weekend.
Rugby.body:
Richie Mo’unga is expecting to face a Wallabies team full of confidence when the All Blacks host their trans-Tasman rivals at Eden Park next weekend. Mo’unga, who has faced the Wallabies a dozen times in his All Blacks career, commended the men from across the ditch for their hard-fought win over the Springboks last weekend as he laid out his expectations for the coming Bledisloe Cup series.

The 42-38 victory was the fifth straight win to begin Les Kiss’ time at the helm of the one-time world champions, and Mo’unga expects it will have put a spring in their step coming into the famed annual series.

Rugby.title: Ardie Savea ends speculation by revealing ‘last dance’ move
Rugby.summary: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea has ended months of speculation about his career, confirming his ‘last dance’ will be with the Blues.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks captain Ardie Savea has ended months of speculation about his career, confirming his “last dance” in Super Rugby Pacific will be with the Blues. Savea teased the announcement for about 40 minutes on a YouTube livestream, before making the move official on Instagram.

Savea played more than 130 Super Rugby matches for the Hurricanes before heading overseas to Japan with the Kobe Kobelco Steelers. The backrower returned to Super Rugby Pacific in 2025 with Moana Pasifika and was named the competition’s Player of the Year.

Rugby.title: Wales wing Adams targets third World Cup
Rugby.summary: Wales wing Josh Adams is nearing full fitness in time for the autumn internationals and looking forward to a World Cup trip to Australia next year.
Rugby.body:
Wales wing Josh Adams says he would love to play in a third World Cup as he targets a first trip to Australia next year. It is exactly a year until Wales play their opening game against Zimbabwe in Adelaide on 2 October, before further pool games against Tonga and England.

"I'm desperate to go, but there is loads of rugby to be played and months ahead of us," said Adams, looking ahead to the tournament. "It is important that you navigate your way through correctly and get to that start line in a good spot to be selected."

Rugby.summary: Dragons backs Anzelo Tuitavuki, Fetuli Paea and Fine Inisi are the latest in a long line of southern hemisphere players to impact Gwent rugby.
Rugby.body:
There was a house at Ebbw Vale's Eugene Cross Park that affectionately became known as The Tongan Embassy. The Pacific Islands influence remains strong in Gwent, to the extent that three Tongans will feature in Dragons' United Rugby Championship (URC) derby against Scarlets in Newport on Saturday (15:00 BST).

Centres Fine Inisi and Fetuli Paea are entering their second seasons with the Rodney Parade club and have been joined by wing Anzelo Tuitavuki. The summer signing made an impressive debut in the round one draw at Benetton.

Rugby.summary: Coach Les Kiss has named a 34-man Wallabies squad that’s bracing for a “formidable challenge” across the ditch.
Rugby.body:
Coach Les Kiss has named a 34-man Wallabies squad that’s bracing for a “formidable challenge” across the ditch, as the All Blacks look to avoid a couple of unwanted feats at their long-standing Eden Park fortress in Auckland.

France were the last team to taste victory over New Zealand at the venue, claiming a three-point win on July 3, 1994. The All Blacks returned to the Garden a month later, starting their still-standing unbeaten run by drawing 18-all with the Springboks.

Rugby.summary: Asian Games Rugby Sevens: Favourites Start Strong on Day One Asia Rugby
Rugby.body:
The leading teams enjoyed successful starts on the opening day of rugby sevens at the Aichi–Nagoya 2026 Asian Games, with Hong Kong China, China, Japan, and Sri Lanka winning both of their men’s matches.

Great weather and an enthusiastic crowd created a lively atmosphere at Nagoya City Mizuho Park Rugby Field. Defending men’s champions Hong Kong China defeated Uzbekistan and Malaysia, scoring 93 points without conceding. China also enjoyed a successful day, beating Malaysia 33–21 before recording a 50–0 victory over Uzbekistan.

Macpherson debuted for the ACT Brumbies at Super Rugby Pacific level in mid-February, in what was the first in a string of appearances off the bench. But the 22-year-old would also earn starts in both the second row and loose forwards.

Rugby.summary: Jack Combes and Alex Post tell BBC Sport about a "dream come true" as they look ahead to the 2027 Rugby World Cup opener against hosts Australia.
Rugby.body:
It is 1 October 2027. There are 61,000 fans inside Perth Stadium. There is a global TV audience in the millions as two teams go through their final warm-ups preparing to open the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

For hosts Australia, twice world champions with a proud rugby history across the codes, it is familiar territory. For their opponents Hong Kong China, it is anything but. It will be their World Cup debut and for their players it will be biggest match of their lives.

Rugby.summary: Ciaran Frawley will make his long-awaited Connacht debut on Friday night after being named at fly-half for Stuart Lancaster's side's URC clash against Benetton in Treviso.
Rugby.body:
Ciaran Frawley will make his long-awaited Connacht debut on Friday night after being named at fly-half for Stuart Lancaster’s side’s URC clash against Benetton in Treviso. The Ireland international was Connacht’s marquee signing of the summer following his move from Leinster, a move that left many blue supporters, and indeed Leo Cullen, disappointed to see him depart.

Viewed as a move that could benefit both player and country, the 28-year-old’s switch to Galway should bring more game time at fly-half and help establish him as a genuine long-term Ireland No.10 option for Andy Farrell.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.summary: With one year to go before the 2027 Rugby World Cup, what lies in wait for Steve Tandy's Wales over the next 12 months before they head to Australia?
Rugby.body:
It might be hard to believe how quickly it comes around, but Thursday marks a year to go until the men's Rugby World Cup begins in Australia. The 2027 competition starts on 1 October in Perth with a match between Australia and Hong Kong China, with the tournament finale on 13 November in Sydney.

Wales are to feature in the second game when they open their campaign against Zimbabwe in Adelaide on 2 October. Steve Tandy's side sit 11th in the world rankings, currently topped by reigning World Cup champions South Africa.

Rugby.summary: Siya Kolisi has been named in the DHL Stormers starting XV for Saturday's United Rugby Championship clash against Edinburgh, just three weeks after featuring in the fourth and final match of Rugby's Great Rivalry.
Rugby.body:
Three weeks after leading South Africa to their ‘Greatest Rivalry’ series-clinching win over New Zealand in Baltimore, double World Cup-winning captain Siya Kolisi will make his second Stormers debut against Edinburgh at The Hive Stadium on Friday.

Kolisi played 118 games for the Cape Town outfit between 2012 and 2020 before two spells at the Sharks, either side of an underwhelming stint with Racing 92 in Paris. The Springbok captain will start at openside flank in what will be his first appearance for the Stormers in six years, following his return to Cape Town.

Rugby.summary: Bristol Bears have suffered a major blow ahead of Saturday evening’s visit from Gallagher PREM champions Northampton Saints, as England and Lions loosehead Ellis Genge will miss the game with a wrist injury.
Rugby.body:
Bristol Bears have suffered a major blow ahead of Saturday evening’s visit from Gallagher PREM champions Northampton Saints, as England and Lions loosehead Ellis Genge will miss the game with a wrist injury.

Genge sustained the injury in the opening minute of the 34-24 win over Sale Sharks in the season opener and played on for more than an hour before asking to be taken off. Bears boss Pat Lam believes Genge, who was playing his first game of the season after an extended rest following international duty in the summer, will be out for only two to three weeks at most.

Rugby.summary: Harlequins back row James Chisholm retires from professional rugby union aged 31, almost two years after rupturing his Achilles.
Rugby.body:
Harlequins back row James Chisholm has retired from professional rugby union aged 31. Chisholm said his recovery from a ruptured Achilles in January 2025 had been "a bit of an uphill battle" and "unfortunately my body just can't get there".

Rugby.summary: Two former players at Melrose’s Greenyards added to Scotland rugby sevens squad The Southern Reporter
Rugby.body:
Two former players at Melrose’s Greenyards have been added to Scotland’s rugby sevens squad. Ex-Southern Knight Freddie Owsley and erstwhile Melrose winger Ross McCann are among four new faces taken on by Borderer Ciaran Beattie’s now-seven-strong full-time contracted squad, the others being Ben Salmon and Lewis Wells.

Their arrival takes the number of ex-Greenyards players in the squad to four as they join another former Knight, Jacob Henry, and prior Melrose scrum-half Roan Frostwick. Henry and Frostwick, both 26, have been kept on from last season’s squad of six, together with Matt Davidson.

Rugby.summary: Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu will play his first match of the new season in Glasgow’s home URC clash with Ulster at Scotstoun on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu will play his first match of the new season in Glasgow’s home URC clash with Ulster at Scotstoun on Saturday. The talismanic centre, who faces a big year ahead leading into the 2027 Rugby World Cup, will have his workload carefully managed across the coming campaign.

But having sat out Warriors’ opening win over Munster in Limerick, Tuipulotu returns this week in one of three changes to the starting XV with Stafford McDowall, who continues to captain the side, switching to outside centre to accommodate Tuipulotu and Ollie Smith dropping out of the 23.

Rugby.title: Isiekwe available after Leicester red rescinded
Rugby.summary: Nick Isiekwe's red card in Saracens' Prem victory at Leicester is rescinded at a disciplinary hearing, meaning he will be available for Sunday's match against Sale.
Rugby.body:
Nick Isiekwe's red card in Saracens' Prem victory at Leicester on Saturday has been rescinded at a disciplinary hearing. The England forward, 28, was shown a 20-minute red card following a high tackle on Tigers full-back Freddie Steward in Sarries' 40-38 win.

Steward provided a statement and live evidence at the hearing, in which he said he did not suspect any foul play by Isiekwe. Steward and Isiekwe both described the head contact as "glancing", a term that the independent panel said it "did not fully accept", although the panel's view was that the degree of force was "low to mid and not high".

Rugby.title: Edinburgh flanker suffers new injury blow as prop backed for Scotland RWC squad
Rugby.summary: Back-rower Ben Muncaster faces a fresh spell on the sidelines as emerging prop Ollie Blyth-Lafferty is handed the chances to press his Scotland claims.
Rugby.body:
The latest injury misfortune to strike the luckless Ben Muncaster will see the Edinburgh back-rower sidelined for 10 weeks, ruling him out of Scotland’s November series of Nations Championship matches.

Muncaster is to undergo surgery on ankle damage he suffered in his comeback outing a fortnight ago in Edinburgh’s final pre-season game against Harlequins. The 24-year-old Scotland cap will miss at least the capital club’s next five games leading into the international window, starting with Friday’s home URC clash with Stormers, and is unlikely to return to action until December.

Rugby.title: Munster statement: CEO Ian Flanagan to step down
Rugby.summary: Munster have confirmed that chief executive Ian Flanagan will step down from his role at the end of October, bringing his tenure at the province to a close.
Rugby.body:
Munster have confirmed that chief executive Ian Flanagan will step down from his role at the end of October, bringing his tenure at the province to a close. Flanagan, who was appointed to the role in 2019, has informed the Munster Rugby Board of his decision, with the IRFU and province announcing that an interim CEO will be appointed in the coming weeks.

A recruitment process for a permanent successor will then begin, leaving Munster with another off-field change as they move through the weeks of the new season. Flanagan’s time in charge included a central role in the development and delivery of Munster’s €7.3m Centre of Excellence in Cork, a long-term investment in player development and the wider game across the province.

Tennis.title: 'Means more than just a trophy'
Tennis.summary: Novak Djokovic claims the 102nd title of his astonishing career as Alex de Minaur retires injured from the China Open final.
Tennis.body:
Novak Djokovic claimed the 102nd title of his astonishing career as Alex de Minaur retired injured from the China Open final. The 39-year-old led De Minaur - a player 12 years his junior - 7-6 (7-3) 0-1 when the Australian was forced to quit with an apparent left thigh problem.

Both players took a medical timeout after a 68-minute first set, but De Minaur managed just one game on their return before shaking hands. It is the 21st year in a row that Djokovic has won at least one singles title.

Tennis.title: Calm in real life but demons on court
Tennis.summary: Daniil Medvedev once said you would need to knock on his hotel door at 6am for seven days in a row to make him angry - but his China Open disqualification was no surprise.
Tennis.body:
Daniil Medvedev once said you would need to knock on his hotel door at 6am for seven days in a row to make him angry. On court, though, he is a far more combustible character who finally ran out of chances when he was disqualified from Monday's China Open semi-final against Novak Djokovic.

Djokovic was serving for a place in the final when the ball ricocheted off the back of the court. Medvedev swiped it into the stands, where it hit a spectator in the face. A few minutes later the Russian was defaulted, as he had to be, under rules that bar a player from "hitting a ball dangerously or recklessly, or with negligent disregard of the consequences."

Tennis.body:
World No 1 Jannik Sinner will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to the knee injury that has kept him on the sidelines since winning Wimbledon. Speaking in a video message on social media, the Italian said: "Me, together with the doctors, have decided that I need a course of treatment for my knee, which means that the 2026 season is officially over.

"The last couple of years gave me so many beautiful feelings and emotions, which this year is going to be way different, but I also need to think about my long-term career so I will do everything possible to get back 100 per cent.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu Is Going to Drop Outside The Top 100 And Yet Her Ranking Tells the Wrong Story
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu Is Going to Drop Outside The Top 100 And Yet Her Ranking Tells the Wrong Story Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
I have been pretty harsh on Emma Raducanu over the years. Some of it, I still think, was more than justified. After all, I was hardly the only voice criticizing her choices. The coaching turnover became ridiculous at times. Some scheduling decisions were impossible to understand. Too often a promising run would be followed by another absence or another reset or another explanation for why the momentum had disappeared.

Five years after winning the US Open, that remains her only professional singles title. There has also occasionally been a tendency around Raducanu to treat perfectly normal progress as evidence that another New York miracle might be just around the corner. It usually wasn't.

Men and women will receive equal prize money at all combined 1,000 events - the highest level of competition outside of the Grand Slams - from next year, the Women's Tennis Association (WTA) has announced.

Events at Indian Wells, California, Miami, Madrid and Beijing already met that commitment, as well as all four Grand Slams. However, the Italian Open, Canadian Open and Cincinnati Open will now also fall into line to meet a long-standing aim of the WTA, at events where men and women both feature.

Golf.summary: You might not realize it, but the offseason is when a lot of the best golfers make their biggest gains. Many of the world’s top players rely on training aids to get there, and they often use them in the same places you and I do: the garage, the gym, a sim room, even the backyard or living room. Training aids are here to stay, and there’s no better proof than the sheer number of top players who use them.

Golf.body:
Former world number one Jon Rahm has said he is quitting LIV Golf, robbing the breakaway circuit of one of its biggest stars while it fights to emerge from bankruptcy. Rahm’s lawyer John Beck told a bankruptcy hearing on Wednesday that the two-time major champion made his decision after looking over details of LIV Golf’s planned next phase.

“Mr Rahm has independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0, as the parties have been referring to it, and has determined that those terms are unacceptable as to him, and he will not be participating going forward in LIV 2.0,” Beck told the court.

Golf.title: Rahm to leave LIV Golf over 'unacceptable' terms
Golf.summary: Jon Rahm will leave LIV Golf after deeming the terms for LIV 2.0 "unacceptable", his lawyer has told a bankruptcy court hearing.
Golf.body:
Jon Rahm will leave LIV Golf after deeming the proposed terms for LIV 2.0 "unacceptable", his lawyer has told a bankruptcy court hearing. The league, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September after Saudi Arabia withdrew its multibillion-dollar funding, has secured a possible $300m in financing from BC Partners Credit in order to try to move forward with the 2027 season.

Rahm's lawyer, John Beck, told the hearing the 31-year-old Spaniard "independently reviewed the terms of LIV 2.0 and determined those terms are unacceptable as to him". It was later said that LIV and Rahm's representatives are "in advanced discussions for a consensual separation agreement between Mr Rahm and LIV".

Golf.title: Patrick Reed had to leave tournament. He shares painful reason why
Golf.summary: Patrick Reed had to withdraw last month from the DP World Tour’s BMW Championship. He shared the painful reason why. The post Patrick Reed had to leave tournament. He shares painful reason why appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Patrick Reed was not thrilled to leave the Wentworth Club last month. It was there where the 2018 Masters winner withdrew with injuries during the second round of the BMW PGA Championship, considered to be the DP World Tour’s showcase event. A day earlier, he was contending after a four-under 68, but was nine over for nine holes when he bowed out.

“Never saw that coming,” Reed said Wednesday ahead of this week’s Spanish Open, his first event since the BMW WD. “It was actually my first time withdrawing during a round of golf due to injury. I mean, I would have rather gone out and shoot a million than actually withdraw.”

About a month before seven lifelong friends and I set off for Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland for an early-September buddies trip, our text-chain chatter shifted from its usual ridiculousness to a gravely serious matter: rainwear. Spurred to action by the wet and windy forecast for the week we’d be on the ground, one of our travel mates alerted us that he’d been bargain-hunting for outerwear at a big-box golf retailer.

Golf.title: An easy way to check your putter aim — and make more putts
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Stephen Sweeney has a simple trick you can use to make sure your putter is aimed where you think it is. The post An easy way to check your putter aim — and make more putts appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
As easy as the pros may make it look, anyone who has ever stepped on a green knows that making putts is no simple task. To get the ball to find the center of the cup, you’ve got to perfectly marry line and speed — not to mention avoiding any imperfections that may throw the ball off line.

As you get closer and closer to the hole, the more important controlling your face angle becomes when putting. On putts that are “makable,” you’ve got to get the ball started on the precise line you intend, which is determined largely by your face angle at impact.

Golf.title: LIV Golf's latest bankruptcy filings call for two significant changes
Golf.summary: LIV Golf's latest bankruptcy filings suggest a different path toward gaining player commitments before this month's deadline. The post LIV Golf’s latest bankruptcy filings call for two significant changes appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
LIV Golf’s vision for LIV 2.0 took a small step forward Monday night when it formalized its restructuring support agreement (RSA) with BC Partners, a London-based private equity firm that has agreed to fund LIV 2.0. On Monday, BC Partners announced an “initial committed investment” as part of a targeted $300 million in cumulative financing to help the league emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy and pursue a future centered on global team golf with a smaller schedule and player equity.

The agreement was filed Monday as part of LIV’s bankruptcy case, and the financing funds require court approval. The league filed for Chapter 11 on Sept. 8, and a hearing is scheduled for Oct. 14. If approved, it would allow the league to move forward with various plans to launch LIV 2.0 in 2027, which would likely include a 10-tournament schedule and half of the events hosted internationally. Monday’s press release marked the first time BC Partners credit head, Ted Goldthorpe, has spoken publicly on the investment.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: If your ball finds a drain, can you take relief on the fairway above it?
Golf.summary: If your ball comes to rest in a drain, is it permissible to take free relief on the fairway above it? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: If your ball finds a drain, can you take relief on the fairway above it? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. A creek runs along the left side of a hole at my course, enters a culvert that runs underneath the fairway and then exits on the right side. Red stakes mark both sides of the creek, but the stakes terminate at the entrance to the culvert where the creek goes underground. My friend claims that if a ball enters the culvert and comes to rest underneath the fairway, the player is entitled to free relief vertically — i.e., directly above the ball onto the fairway. His reasoning is that because the red stakes terminate at the entrance to the culvert, the portion of the creek inside the culvert is no longer part of the marked penalty area. I called BS on this. Isn’t the ball still considered in the penalty area while it is inside the culvert? Regardless, is there any rule that would allow a player to take free relief directly above the ball onto the fairway? —W. Scott Clark, via email

F. Scott — sorry, W. Scott (Rules Guy must have Fitzgerald on his mind) — there are some nuances here that potentially complicate matters, which we will pointedly ignore, so fusspots please spare us your letters….

Golf.title: LIV Golf secures potential $300m investment for 2027 season
Golf.summary: LIV Golf secures potential $300m investment for 2027 season golfbusinessnews.com
Golf.body:
LIV Golf has announced that it has secured $300m in financing from BC Partners Credit in order to try to move forward with the 2027 season. The league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September after Saudi Arabia’s Public Invest Fund withdrew its multibillion-dollar funding, starting a court-supervised restructuring process that they hope to complete in early 2027.

Chapter 11 protection postpones a US company’s obligations to its creditors, giving it time to reorganise its debts or sell parts of the business. PIF is providing a bankruptcy loan of $49.6m (£36.6m) – called ‘debtor in possession’ financing – to help fund the process.

Golf.title: LIV Golf gets $300M lifeline for 2027 relaunch after Saudi funding was pulled
Golf.summary: LIV Golf gets $300M lifeline for 2027 relaunch after Saudi funding was pulled lbc.co.uk
Golf.body:
LIV Golf has secured an initial funding commitment for a potential 300 million US dollars (£227m) investment from BC Partners Credit to help relaunch in 2027. The breakaway series filed for bankruptcy last month after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund – which had spent 5bn USD (£3.7bn) in four years – announced it was withdrawing support at the end of the season.

That cast the future of LIV into doubt but a deal with BC, subject to approval from the bankruptcy court, gives it the chance to reset next year. BC signed a term sheet with LIV last month, requiring it to sign half of the players to whom it owes money, as part of its financing plan.

Golf.title: LIV Golf makes HUGE announcement as 2027 deadline looms
Golf.summary: LIV Golf makes HUGE announcement as 2027 deadline looms Today's Golfer
Golf.body:
LIV Golf has secured initial funding for its 2.0 era. In a statement released on Monday, BC Partners Credit announced an “initial committed investment in LIV Golf”. It added that it is the first part of a targeted $300 million in cumulative financing to help LIV Golf emerge from its restructuring as a fiscally strong, sustainable, team-focused golf league that complements the existing professional tours and contributes to the long-term potential of the sport”.

As part of the agreement, the deadline for players to commit to LIV’s future has been delayed. LIV filed for a Chapter 11 bankruptcy last month with claims that its ‘2.0’ era will be see the league become player-owned from 2027. CEO Scott O’Neil also promised to keep events “in places like Australia, South Africa, Mexico, England, Hong Kong, and the United States”, as well as a field expansion to 75 players with a halfway cut and additional qualification pathways – including Monday qualifiers.

Golf.title: Former PGA Tour staple course finds new home as part of LPGA's new Hawaii swing
Golf.summary: The Plantation Course at Kapalua was a PGA Tour staple for 25 years. That relationship ended, but it now has a new one with the LPGA. The post Former PGA Tour staple course finds new home as part of LPGA’s new Hawaii swing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Plantation Course at Kapalua was a PGA Tour staple for 25 years, hosting the Sentry, which served as the kickoff event from 1999 to 2013 and again from 2024 to 2025. That relationship ended in April when the PGA Tour announced it planned to end its tournament presence in Maui.

But while the PGA Tour won’t be returning to the Plantation Course next year, Kapalua now has a new professional golf partner in the LPGA. On Monday, the LPGA announced that the Lotte Championship will be hosted at the Plantation Course starting in 2027. The tournament, which Jeeno Thitikul won on Sunday, will now be held in March as part of a two-tournament Hawaii Swing along with the recently announced Nanea Cup. The Lotte Championship will have a $3 million purse next season.

Golf.title: At Bank of Utah, the PGA Tour's different fall chases were on display
Golf.summary: Austin Smotherman won the day at the Bank of Utah Championship. but he wasn't the only winner of the PGA Tour's second fall event. The post At Bank of Utah, the PGA Tour’s different fall chases were on display appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Doug Ghim smiled as Austin Smotherman gazed into the Utah sky after winning his first PGA Tour event in 100 starts. There was no pain in Ghim’s face after his attempt to win his first title in 192 starts came up short. There was just gratitude that he’s still grinding and chasing his dreams on the top golf circuit in the world.

“It’s what we play for; it’s what we practice for,” Ghim said after finishing two shots behind Smotherman on Sunday at the Bank of Utah Championship. “Obviously the money and the points are great, but as a little kid trying to win a PGA Tour event, just a chance to do that is a dream come true. … We used to get really excited just to play courses that pros played at, and to think that as a 30-year-old, to have done this for my seventh season and to get an opportunity like today and what I’ve had in the past and hopefully more in the future, it’s such a privilege.

Golf.summary: Austin Smotherman won the 2026 Bank of Utah Championship for his first PGA Tour win. Here's a breakdown of what's in his winning golf bag. The post Austin Smotherman WITB: Bank of Utah winner carries 7-year-old hybrid appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Austin Smotherman finally broke through Sunday, winning his first PGA Tour title at the Bank of Utah Championship. Aside from deals with L.A.B. Golf for his putter and Titleist for the Pro V1x, Smotherman is a gear free agent, free to play whatever golf clubs he wants.

One of those clubs is a nearly seven-year-old TaylorMade SIM Max 3-hybrid, making him just the fourth player this season to win on the PGA Tour with a hybrid. The SIM Max rescue is one of the more famous TaylorMade hybrids of the past decade, mainly because it’s one of the last to get serious play on the PGA Tour.

Golf.title: The unauthorized blueprint to save U.S. golf's match play kryptonite
Golf.summary: The blueprint to saving American team golf already exists ... and it comes to us courtesy of a major Olympic sport. The post The unauthorized blueprint to save U.S. golf’s match play kryptonite appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you were to summarize the 2020s for American team golf, your words probably wouldn’t be very friendly. Well, unless you were a member of the team’s leadership, in which case your words to explain why the team has so frequently underwhelmed expectations might be a little too friendly.

E.g.: The conditions at Bethpage Black weren’t what the Americans expected … even though the team controlled the course setup. In Rome, a five-week layoff after the Tour Championship was too long for the team to stay sharp. And then there’s this one, also from Bethpage: Scottie Scheffler was sent out on the wrong set of holes in foursomes, forcing the World No. 1 to engineer a switch before his second alternate shot match of the weekend.

Golf.title: Austin Smotherman's Bank of Utah Championship win was a story 10 years in the making
Golf.summary: In his 100th career PGA Tour start, Austin Smotherman finally achieved a lifelong dream in Utah. It was a golf story 10 years in the making. The post Austin Smotherman’s Bank of Utah Championship win was a story 10 years in the making appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Back in March, Austin Smotherman entered Sunday at the Cognizant Championship on the precipice of his dream. Holding the 54-hole lead in a PGA Tour event for the first time in his career, the then-31-year-old faced the most terrifying round of his career. He navigated PGA National well enough that Sunday, but finished T2 as Nico Echavarria claimed the title after Shane Lowry imploded. But after he tapped in to close out his day, Smotherman looked like a man who had just won.

Because he knew that was a necessary step to get to where he eventually wanted to go. “This was kind of just my first really big pedestal,” Smotherman said that Sunday. “Kind of had a back door-ish top 5 in the Mexico Open at Vidanta a couple years ago, and never really had the same kind of moments coming down the stretch … This will be a week I always look back at.”

Golf.title: Titleist begins 2027 Pro V1 tour seeding at Baycurrent Classic
Golf.summary: As Monday arrives in Japan, Titleist officially announces the PGA Tour launch of the new 2027 Pro V1 and Pro V1x golf balls. The post Titleist begins 2027 Pro V1 tour seeding at Baycurrent Classic appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Sunday night in the United States means it’s already Monday morning in Japan, and Titleist is getting a head start on what will surely be this week’s biggest gear story. This week’s Baycurrent Championship at Yokohama Country Club will officially launch Titleist’s new 2027 Pro V1 and Pro V1x golf balls.

The company is staying quiet on the technical details, which will come with the ball’s retail launch, likely in January or February if traditional launch cadences hold. The new golf balls first hit the USGA Conforming list three weeks ago at the Biltmore Championship, and several PGA Tour players have already made the switch. That was the result of a lengthy Tour feedback process by Titleist’s R&D team.

Golf.title: Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: LIV Golf’s Adrian Meronk outlasts Casey Jarvis to claim victory at St Andrews
Golf.summary: Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: LIV Golf’s Adrian Meronk outlasts Casey Jarvis to claim victory at St Andrews Sky Sports
Golf.body:
Adrian Meronk came from four shots behind to overtake Casey Jarvis and win the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship by two strokes on a gripping final day at St Andrews. The victory saw the LIV Golfer end a 1,078-day wait to claim his fifth DP World Tour title and regain his tour card for next season, as he wrapped up his week with a four-under 68.

Jarvis held a two-stroke lead coming into day four at St Andrews, and following a fast start that included back-to-back birdies on holes four and five, he slumped, making bogeys on holes nine and 11.

Golf.title: 'Lost for words': Adrian Meronk's emotional St. Andrews win led to a LIV question
Golf.summary: Adrian Meronk's emotions came out after an important win at St. Andrews. Then came a question about LIV Golf and his future. The post ‘Lost for words’: Adrian Meronk’s emotional St. Andrews win led to a LIV question appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Adrian Meronk’s professional career started at the Home of Golf, when he made his pro debut on the DP World Tour at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship in 2016. Ten years later, Meronk broke down in scoring at The Old Course as he watched Casey Jarvis fail to make an eagle from the Valley of Sin to give him the title.

“It’s unreal,” an emotional Meronk said after the win. “I never usually cry but this one feels really special. I’m sorry, I’m just lost for words. To win here after 10 years, after turning pro, it’s a dream come true, and it’s unusual. I’m sorry, I’m at a loss for words, but I’m extremely happy and relieved.”

Golf.title: LIV Golf’s Adrian Meronk holds nerve to win Alfred Dunhill Links Championship
Golf.summary: LIV Golf’s Adrian Meronk holds nerve to win Alfred Dunhill Links Championship Irish Examiner
Golf.body:
LIV Golf’s Adrian Meronk held his nerve over a blustery Old Course at St Andrews to claim a two-shot victory in the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship. The 33-year-old Pole – among the DP World Tour members allowed to play in conflicting LIV Golf tournaments under the 2026 Conditional Release Agreement – made the most of overnight leader Casey Jarvis seeing his challenge fade to finish with a 68 for a 20-under total.

Meronk, who had shot a nine-under 63 in his third round at Kingsbarns, made a fast start in the penultimate group with three birdies in the opening five holes, holing from 35 feet at the first, before a bogey on the seventh, which was soon recovered on the ninth.

Golf.title: World number 979 Stewart's dilemma after finishing fourth at Alfred Dunhill Links
Golf.summary: Scotland's Michael Stewart has a choice to make after securing his best finish at a DP World Tour event.
Golf.body:
On Wednesday, Michael Stewart earned £2,500 for finishing runner-up in the Tartan Pro Tour event at Duddingston Golf Club near Edinburgh. Four days later, the world number 979 has just picked up nearly 100 times that by finishing joint fourth behind winner Adrian Meronk at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

But what the 36-year-old Scot regards as "without doubt" the best week of his career has left him with a dilemma. Finishing in the top 10 - two shots behind Poland's Meronk, one behind Denmark's Niklas Norgaard and South Africa's Casey Jarvis, and tied with England's Tommy Fleetwood - means he qualifies for next week's big-money Spanish Open.

Golf.title: DP World Tour Warns LIV Golf Refugees About Returning
Golf.summary: DP World Tour Warns LIV Golf Refugees About Returning Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
The DP World Tour has sent a clear message to LIV Golf players hoping to return after the breakaway league filed for bankruptcy. A tour spokesperson confirmed they see a surge in interest from players seeking a route back to Europe. However, any comeback requires meeting strict conditions. Players must be free of conflicting contracts and agree to follow existing membership rules. They might also lose access to the lucrative Rolex Series events. This stance comes as LIV Golf faces an uncertain future with its Chapter 11 filing in New Jersey.

Only 10 days remain for LIV players to determine whether they remain with the breakaway circuit or return to the DP World Tour or PGA Tour. The tour is exploring ways to accommodate these returning players, but it will not be automatic. Those who left for LIV before the bankruptcy are already facing hurdles. The tour granted conditional releases to eight members in February, including Tyrrell Hatton and Thomas Detry. These players agreed to pay fines and play extra tournaments to return without further punishment.

Golf.summary: Report: LIV Golf secure enough player support for 2027 plans Golfmagic
Golf.body:
LIV Golf have received verbal commitments from enough players to press ahead with their plans for 2027, according to a report. Industry sources told Golf Channel that a significant number of players have committed to the proposed new version of the circuit, putting LIV comfortably above the threshold required to secure future funding.

Golf.title: The key move that boosts swing speed — and the tool that can help train it
Golf.summary: Learn how the Why Golf Power Plate can help you improve your weight shift, boost ball contact and create more power in your swing. The post The key move that boosts swing speed — and the tool that can help train it appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you’re looking for more speed and better contact, the answer isn’t just to swing harder. A big part of the equation is learning how to move pressure through your feet and into your lead side before impact. When that sequence is right, it becomes easier to deliver the club with a stable lower body, find the center of the face and compress the ball instead of catching it fat or thin. That’s the idea behind Why Golf’s Power Plate.

The training aid sets your feet on a slight incline, giving you an exaggerated feel for a proper weight shift in your swing. First, the incline makes it easier to shift your weight back into your trail leg. Then the goal is simple: move that pressure into your lead side without letting your body slide away from the target.

It all boils down to narrowing your focus.

Tom Kim’s last PGA Tour win, which came at the co-sanctioned Genesis Scottish Open in July, ended with a congratulatory text from Tiger Woods. On Saturday, as Kim prepared for a career-altering round at the 2026 Asian Games, Woods sent him a different message.

“Just be you. Nothing more, nothing less,” the message from Woods said, via Korea’s Yonhap News Agency. Kim arrived in Japan for this week’s Asian Games under immense pressure. South Korean men between the ages of 18 and 35 are required to serve up to 21 months in the defense forces. PGA Tour pros Sangmoon Bae and Seung-yul Noh served during their prime and it impacted their golf. But the South Korean government awards exemptions to athletes who win a gold medal at the Asian Games or any of the three medals at the Olympics. Si Woo Kim and Sunjae Im won a gold medal in the team competition at the 2023 Asian Games, earning an exemption from military service.

Golf.title: This talented mid-am is lovingly called 'Blandy.' Although he's anything but
Golf.summary: Andrew Davidson is lovingly called “Blandy.” But he’s anything but, and he’s one of the players in next week’s Bridges Cup. The post This talented mid-am is lovingly called ‘Blandy.’ Although he’s anything but appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Andrew Davidson does appreciate one view of his nickname. You don’t mind being called it in golf, because being it can be beautiful in golf. Basic pars are your friends. And a few years back, during one streak while at the University of Stirling, Davidson signed for them a lot.

He shot even par eight straight rounds, so of course his pals had to come up with something to call him other than “Andrew.” Thing is, though, it’s also a touch ironic. Most everything about the 32-year-old is decidedly un-bland. He is, in fact, accomplished at golf, and next week, he’ll be one of a dozen International players who will meet the American side at the Bridges Cup, a mid-amateur team event that’ll be played this year at Trump Turnberry, in Davidson’s home country of Scotland. Davidson’s list of golf achievements is long. He’s represented his country at the Home Internationals, the European Team Championship and the European Nations Cup. He’s won the Scottish order of merit. He’s a winner of the Welsh Amateur Stroke Play. He’s a winner of the Battle Trophy and East of Scotland Championship. He’s a two-time Scottish Area team champion.

Golf.title: LIV Golf’s Bankruptcy Plan Relies On Player Equity Swap
Golf.summary: LIV Golf’s Bankruptcy Plan Relies On Player Equity Swap Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
LIV Golf is filing for Chapter 11 protection after its Saudi backers cut off funding in April. The league owes millions in unpaid player salaries and legal fees. A new deal requires players to swap their unpaid cash for a majority ownership stake in the reorganized business. This move marks a desperate pivot from a cash-rich startup to a player-owned entity struggling to survive.

The financial math is stark. During the 90 days preceding bankruptcy, Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher received over $7.1 million from LIV Golf solely for legal fees. The firm agreed to discount its bills by 20% but still collected a massive sum. Meanwhile, the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, which spent over $5 billion trying to reshape pro golf, stopped writing checks. The league entered court with roughly $15 million in cash but faced a secured debt facility of approximately $495 million. That gap is too wide to bridge without a radical restructuring.

Golf.body:
-11 C Jarvis (RSA); -10 M Jordan (Eng), M. J. Daffue (RSA), R Repetto Taylor (Esp) Defending champion Robert MacIntyre took advantage of calm conditions at Kingsbarns to shoot 65 and charge into contention at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

The Scot's round of seven under left him in a tie for ninth place, three strokes behind halfway leader Casey Jarvis of South Africa. England's Matthew Jordan matched MacIntyre's score of 72 with six birdies and an eagle at Carnoustie to sit on 10 under for the tournament.

Golf.title: LIV Golf’s In-House Lawyers Remain as Gibson Dunn Discounts Fees
Golf.summary: LIV Golf’s In-House Lawyers Remain as Gibson Dunn Discounts Fees Bloomberg Law News
Golf.body:
LIV Golf Inc. paid more than $7.1 million to Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher in discounted legal fees as the once Saudi Arabian-backed professional golf circuit was shedding much of its workforce, according to bankruptcy court records.

LIV began laying off most of its employees in August, but almost all its in-house legal staff, including chief legal officer John Ruzich, have agreed to remain with the business through October, said three sources familiar with LIV’s operations. The company’s agreement with private equity firm BC Partners Advisors LP, which is backing LIV’s move to restructure through the Chapter 11 process, would require that at least 50% of its players convert their unpaid compensation into a majority equity stake in the reorganized business.

Golf.title: From Pine Valley to Trump Turnberry, golf keeps taking Andrew Price places
Golf.summary: For Team USA Bridges Cup competitor Andrew Price, golf has taken him to places he only used to dream about. The post From Pine Valley to Trump Turnberry, golf keeps taking Andrew Price places appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
For Andrew Price, the best part of golf might not be the pars and birdies — it’s where the game takes him. Price, 44, grew up in Lake Forest, Ill., playing just about every sport he could. Basketball, baseball and golf among them. By the time he reached high school, though, it was clear golf was the sport that would take him furthest. After a successful junior career, Price played collegiately at Kansas, competing for a top-25 program and building friendships that have lasted a lifetime.

But the real journey was just beginning. After college, Price spent a couple of years in Arizona before returning home to Chicagoland, where he eventually settled back in the suburbs, joining his family’s fourth-generation insurance business, leaving him time on the side to get his game in shape for amateur events. What started with events like the Western Amateur and USGA qualifiers gradually opened doors to the highest levels of mid-amateur golf. And with each new opportunity came another unforgettable experience.

Golf.title: Sergio Garcia moves to end LIV Golf contract amid league’s uncertainty
Golf.summary: Sergio Garcia moves to end LIV Golf contract amid league’s uncertainty Irish Golfer Magazine
Golf.body:
Sergio Garcia has taken formal steps to exit his LIV Golf deal, filing a motion in bankruptcy court to terminate the contract as the breakaway league battles for its future, according to recent court filings.

The court documents, first reported by the Financial Times, show the Spaniard is seeking clarity on his status while LIV fights for survival. The move comes after the league lost financial backing from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) in April, leaving serious doubts over its 2027 schedule.

Golf.title: Tom Kim charges into lead in bid to avoid military service
Golf.summary: PGA Tour pro Tom Kim needs to win gold at the 2026 Asian Games to avoid mandatory military service. With 18 holes to go, he's in the lead. The post Tom Kim charges into lead in bid to avoid military service appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Shortly after his singles match ended last Sunday at the 2026 Presidents Cup, Tom Kim quickly got on a plane to Japan. That the Presidents Cup hadn’t officially ended didn’t matter to him.

Awaiting Kim at Japan’s Kasugai Country Club was what could very well be the most important tournament of his entire career: the 2026 Asian Games. Why is the event so crucial for Kim, who already has four PGA Tour wins on his resume? Because if he or his South Korean team finish with the gold medal this week, Kim will be exempted from nearly two years of mandatory military service.

Technology has been encroaching on the golf world for years. Even two of the oldest and most revered courses in the world have been impacted by the digital age. At least that was the case on Thursday at the 2026 Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, the annual DP World Tour event played at the Old Course at St. Andrews, Carnoustie and Kingsbarns.

It was at Carnoustie, host of eight Open Championships, that one widespread piece of modern technology ticked off one of the top pro golfers in the world. The technological device in question was a TV drone, and the golfer in question was Scotland’s own Robert MacIntyre.

Golf.title: He sold shirts at this year’s U.S. Open. Next year, he'll be playing in it
Golf.summary: Andrew Bailey, a sales manager for a golf-apparel company, won the U.S. Mid-Amateur on Thursday, earning a spot in the 2027 U.S. Open. The post He sold shirts at this year’s U.S. Open. Next year, he’ll be playing in it appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Andrew Bailey, a 34-year-old sales manager at golf-apparel company Holderness & Bourne, didn’t have to be at the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills. He chose to be, volunteering his time to help out his brand in the hulking merchandise center.

Bailey also will be in attendance at next year’s U.S. Open at Pebble Beach — but in a markedly different capacity: as one of the 156 players in the field. Bailey’s rags- … well, quarter-zips-to-riches story became a reality Thursday when he won the 45th U.S. Mid-Amateur at Sand Valley Resort in Nekoosa, Wis., defeating Nate Smith, 5 and 4, in the 36-hole final.

Golf.title: Sergio Garcia files to have LIV Golf contract terminated
Golf.summary: Sergio Garcia files to have LIV Golf contract terminated RTE.ie
Golf.body:
Sergio Garcia is pursuing the termination of his LIV Golf contract, a potential path out of the league. As LIV Golf works toward fulfilling a restructuring agreement following Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, Garcia's attorney argued in a six-page courtfiling on Wednesday that termination "should not be objectionable" to the league because it "is consistent with (LIV Golf's) statement that the agreement is 'not part of (LIV Golf's) go-forward business plan.'"

The Spaniard's camp further argued that with the contract still in place, "tournament organisers, sponsors and other counterparties may hesitate before dealing with Garcia, who may be unable to represent that they are free of competing contractual commitments".

In the wake of the U.S. team’s thrilling comeback in Sunday singles to notch a 17-13 victory over the Internationals at the Presidents Cup, questions remain about the Americans’ performance in the team-match portion of the event — particularly in the foursomes format.

Foursomes — or alternate shot — has been difficult for the U.S. team in recent years. At this year’s Presidents Cup, the U.S. team went 2-7 in foursomes. And last year’s Ryder Cup at Bethpage Black was no better, with the U.S. going 2-6-0 against the Europeans.

Here’s the truth about George Washington, the president who could not tell a lie: He left the country exactly once. That lone trip was to Barbados, where he spent six weeks in a house that bears his name today.

Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Doug Spencer ran an experiment to find out if a bump-and-run is really more reliable than a chip shot. The post Is the bump-and-run *really* more reliable than a chip shot? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Ditching high-loft wedges around the green in favor of a hybrid bump-and-run is one of golf’s classic pieces of advice, but do the numbers actually back it up? That was something I wondered recently, so I decided to conduct a small experiment.

We put three amateur players through a 30-shot test to see if putting with a hybrid produces better proximity and consistency than traditional wedge options. And not only did they test their mettle on both types of shots, when it came to the hybrid bump-and-run, this was their first time ever trying the shot.

Golf.title: Sergio Garcia seeks exit from LIV Golf contract, while LIV Golf Australia venue says it hasn't been paid in court filings
Golf.summary: Sergio Garcia seeks exit from LIV Golf contract, while LIV Golf Australia venue says it hasn't been paid in court filings Golf Digest
Golf.body:
Sergio Garcia is seeking official termination of his LIV Golf contract, according to new court filings. Last month, LIV Golf’s bankruptcy plea included a restructuring that would likely release LIV players from their existing contracts, allowing them to pursue opportunities elsewhere. Late Wednesday, Garcia’s lawyers and his LLC (Even Par) asserted they do not oppose this motion but do want clarification, as Garcia’s representation requests the court honor the request to end the agreement or allow Garcia to end it. As currently constructed, Garcia argues, the deal is confusing.

“So long as the Agreement remains of record, tournament organizers, sponsors, and other counterparties may hesitate before dealing with Garcia, who may be unable to represent that they are free of competing contractual commitments,” Garcia’s lawyers argue. “That uncertainty is particularly acute for a professional athlete, whose tournament schedule, sponsorship arrangements, and participation in other events must be planned well in advance, and whose competitive career is necessarily finite.”

Badminton.title: Ten Reputable PVC Sports Flooring Manufacturers in China: A 2026 BWF Review
Badminton.summary: Ten Reputable PVC Sports Flooring Manufacturers in China: A 2026 BWF Review EIN Presswire
Badminton.body:
CALIFORNIA, CA, UNITED STATES, October 8, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- WUXI, Jiangsu, China — October 8, 2026 A 2026 capability review of China’s commercial PVC flooring industry has assessed ten manufacturers, headed by Wuxi Tefa Decoration Material Co., Ltd., the Jiangsu-based producer that markets homogeneous vinyl flooring, PVC sports flooring and aircraft flooring under the Farfly Flying Flooring brand. The review compares product portfolios, third-party certification documentation, manufacturing capacity, export service and after-sales support, and sets out the evidence buyers should demand when a supplier claims Badminton World Federation (BWF) certification for sports flooring.

The review draws on documentation supplied by Wuxi Tefa — including ISO management system certificates, CE and EN test reports, and civil aviation combustion and smoke-toxicity records — together with publicly available registration and product information for the other nine manufacturers. Figures attributed to individual suppliers other than Wuxi Tefa were not independently audited by the authors of this review, and certification status should be confirmed directly with the issuing body before any order is placed.

Badminton.title: World Juniors: Indonesia Survive UAE Jolt, Make Semis
Badminton.summary: World Juniors: Indonesia Survive UAE Jolt, Make Semis BWF
Badminton.body:
Indonesia survived a first set scare from United Arab Emirates to progress into the semifinals of the VICTOR BWF World Junior Team Championships 2026. After their upset of India in the group playoff, UAE produced yet another sensational performance in punching above their weight against the two-time champions. Played in a hypnotic atmosphere with hundreds of Indonesian fans singing and cheering on their team, the quarterfinal tie saw UAE take the fight to their far higher rated opponents.

Riyan Malhan was yet again UAE’s talisman, as he reduced a 4-11 deficit to 20-22 by the end of the second match. He then returned with Adam Jeslin for the men’s doubles with UAE trailing 37-44 and the two very nearly took the match from Raihan Pramono/Anju Siahaan. At 53-all, they scored what they thought was a winner for match point, only for a fault to be called. The Indonesians then took the first set 55-54.

Badminton.body:
Last month, Riyan Malhan made history becoming the first UAE player to win a Badminton Asia title by claiming the Under-17 crown at the Badminton Asia Junior Championships. A year ago, aged just 15, Malhan caused a flutter at the BWF World Junior Championships 2025 by making the Round of 16. Since then Malhan has gone from strength to strength – some of his notable achievements include titles at the Hungarian Junior and Ghana International, besides a silver at the Slovak Junior last November.

Having won the Asian title (he also won bronze in men’s doubles with Adam Jeslin) just ahead of his second World Juniors, Malhan arrived in Cairo confident of a strong performance.

Badminton.summary: Debutants Cyprus Relish Opening Experience BWF
Badminton.body:
It wasn’t a bad debut for Cyprus at the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026. Three-time champions Korea did beat them comfortably but the first-timers registered their presence as the 22nd edition of the Suhandinata Cup got underway at the Cairo International Stadium.

Coach Shai Geffen was pleased with his team’s performance against the Asian powerhouse. “This is a big opportunity,” said Geffen. “It’s a first time for us participating in any World Championships as a team. So this is a good opportunity for the players to understand the culture of badminton – not just in Europe. We could play Korea, a powerhouse of Asia, and we’ll play Denmark, one of the best teams in the world. So this is a big challenge. But to see where we are and how we can improve.

Badminton.body:
Exactly a year ago, Azerbaijan’s Ulvi Huseynov was going on court for his men’s singles final at a regional championships when he felt an inexplicable heaviness in his right shoulder while picking up his racket bag.

He did lose that match, and he remembers how quiet the team bus was on their way back to the hotel. He was asked to leave for home immediately, and only on getting there did he realise why the management had insisted he skip the prize ceremony later that day – his father had passed away.

Badminton.title: ‘It’s a Dream Coming True’
Badminton.summary: ‘It’s a Dream Coming True’ BWF
Badminton.body:
Egypt is on the cusp of making history, and Hadia Hosny couldn’t be happier. Cairo plays host to the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026 – the biggest tournament ever held in the country. The three-time Olympian, former Member of the Egyptian Parliament, and now the President of the Egyptian Badminton Federation, talks of the significance of hosting the tournament:

What does it mean for you to have a tournament of this scale in Egypt? This is the first time ever we’re having a very big tournament like this. It means a lot. I was wishing this since I was an athlete and I feel like I’m the one on court right now (laughs).

Badminton.title: Suhandinata Cup Redraw: Korea Grouped With Denmark
Badminton.summary: Suhandinata Cup Redraw: Korea Grouped With Denmark BWF
Badminton.body:
Three-time champions Korea are grouped with European power Denmark at the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026 that will start in Cairo on Monday 5 October. The redraw for the World Junior Championships, necessitated by the withdrawals of Nigeria and Macau China after the original draw in August, was held today.

Korea, Denmark and debutants Cyprus are in Group H2, while Group H1 has second seeds Thailand, debutants Senegal, and Brazil. Defending champions China, the 5/8 seeds, are in Group E1 with South Africa and Zambia; Group E2 consists of Turkiye, Mauritius and Zimbabwe.

Badminton.title: Humans of Shuttle Time: Joshua Muguluma Richard
Badminton.summary: Humans of Shuttle Time: Joshua Muguluma Richard BWF
Badminton.body:
This is the 75th story in our Humans of Shuttle Time series, in which we present the perspectives of those who are involved with badminton at the grassroots level. Joshua Muguluma Richard, Shuttle Time Tutor with Uganda Badminton Association, talks of his journey in badminton.

I was born in Uganda, Kampala as the second of three boys. My childhood was shaped by simple living with strong family values and support from my parents. Growing up, I learned the importance of respect, hard work, and kindness from people around me. My social background was influenced a lot by the community I lived in, especially my neighbours who knew each other well and often helped one another during difficult times.
